import Mathlib

/-!
# Erdős Problem #287 — elementary structural package (definitions)

This file sets up the basic definitions used throughout the package:

* the top `p`-adic layer of a finite set `A` of positive integers whose reciprocals sum to `1`;
* a kernel-reducing computation of the reduced numerator of `∑_{s∈S} 1/s`
  together with the "largest numerator" quantity `C`.

All of the "structural" theorems live in the sibling files.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace Erdos287

/-! ## Top `p`-adic layer -/

/-- The maximal `p`-adic valuation attained over a finite set `A`. -/
def topExp (A : Finset ℕ) (p : ℕ) : ℕ := A.sup (fun a => Nat.factorization a p)

/-- The top `p`-adic layer: the elements of `A` whose `p`-adic valuation is maximal. -/
def topLayer (A : Finset ℕ) (p : ℕ) : Finset ℕ :=
  A.filter (fun a => Nat.factorization a p = topExp A p)

lemma mem_topLayer {A : Finset ℕ} {p a : ℕ} :
    a ∈ topLayer A p ↔ a ∈ A ∧ Nat.factorization a p = topExp A p := by
  simp [topLayer]

lemma topLayer_subset (A : Finset ℕ) (p : ℕ) : topLayer A p ⊆ A := by
  intro a ha; exact (mem_topLayer.1 ha).1

/-! ## Computable reduced-numerator machinery

We compute the reduced numerator of `∑_{s∈S} 1/s` with a kernel-reducing fold
so that the values of `C` can be certified with `decide` (never `native_decide`).
-/

/-- One step of reduced-fraction addition on `(numerator, denominator)` pairs. -/
def addF (x y : ℤ × ℕ) : ℤ × ℕ :=
  let n := x.1 * (y.2 : ℤ) + y.1 * (x.2 : ℤ)
  let d := x.2 * y.2
  let g := Nat.gcd n.natAbs d
  (n / (g : ℤ), d / g)

/-- The reduced `(numerator, denominator)` pair of `∑_{s∈l} 1/s` for a list `l`. -/
def sumP (l : List ℕ) : ℤ × ℕ :=
  l.foldr (fun s acc => addF acc (1, s)) (0, 1)

/-- The reduced numerator of `∑_{s∈l} 1/s`. -/
def numOf (l : List ℕ) : ℤ := (sumP l).1

/-- The reduced denominator of `∑_{s∈l} 1/s`. -/
def denOf (l : List ℕ) : ℕ := (sumP l).2

/-- The largest reduced numerator of `∑_{s∈S} 1/s` over nonempty subsets
`S ⊆ {1,…,j}`, computed over the sublists of `[1,…,j]`. -/
def C (j : ℕ) : ℤ :=
  ((((List.range j).map (· + 1)).sublists.filter (fun l => l ≠ [])).map numOf).foldr max 0

end Erdos287

@@END_FILE@@
@@BEGIN_FILE bytes=5206 sha256=c3dfcd30b21b16d47713887e88ef82d1f9ba93f768a42f929f513b5ea10a1613 path=LEAN_PROJECT/RequestProject/Erdos287/Direct/AbsorberInterfaces.lean@@
import RequestProject.Erdos287.Direct.TargetTuningFinite

/-!
# Route D — the exact signed absorber interface

INTERNAL #287 RESEARCH PROGRAMME ONLY.  **Erdős #287 is `OPEN` here and is not claimed.**

For a finite family of signed rational increments `ξ_i` put

`D_buf = lcm_i den(ξ_i)`,  `b_buf = gcd_i (D_buf · ξ_i)`.

Kernel-proved here are the **necessary lattice conditions** for a residual `e` to be an exact
signed combination of the increments:

* `D_buf · e` is an integer (`bufDen_mul_mem_int`);
* `b_buf ∣ D_buf · e` (`absorber_lattice_necessary`).

The predicate `ExactSignedAbsorber`, expressing a bounded binary selection of *physically
compatible* protected switches realising the residual exactly, is defined and **deliberately
not inhabited**.  Its status is `OPEN`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace Erdos287
namespace Direct

/-! ## D.35  Buffer denominator and buffer gcd -/

/-- The buffer denominator `D_buf = lcm_i den(ξ_i)`. -/
def bufDen {ι : Type*} (S : Finset ι) (xi : ι → ℚ) : ℕ := S.lcm (fun i => (xi i).den)

/-- The integer `D · r`, valid when `den r ∣ D`. -/
def carryNum (D : ℕ) (r : ℚ) : ℤ := ((D / r.den : ℕ) : ℤ) * r.num

/-- **`carryNum_spec`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  `carryNum` really computes `D · r` whenever the
denominator divides `D`. -/
theorem carryNum_spec {D : ℕ} {r : ℚ} (h : r.den ∣ D) : ((carryNum D r : ℤ) : ℚ) = (D : ℚ) * r := by
  obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := h
  rw [carryNum, Nat.mul_div_cancel_left _ (Nat.pos_of_ne_zero r.den_nz)]
  push_cast
  calc (k : ℚ) * (r.num : ℚ) = (k : ℚ) * ((r.den : ℚ) * r) := by rw [Rat.den_mul_eq_num]
    _ = (r.den : ℚ) * (k : ℚ) * r := by ring

theorem den_dvd_bufDen {ι : Type*} {S : Finset ι} {xi : ι → ℚ} {i : ι} (hi : i ∈ S) :
    (xi i).den ∣ bufDen S xi := Finset.dvd_lcm hi

/-- The buffer gcd `b_buf = gcd_i (D_buf · ξ_i)`. -/
def bufGcd {ι : Type*} (S : Finset ι) (xi : ι → ℚ) : ℤ :=
  S.gcd (fun i => carryNum (bufDen S xi) (xi i))

theorem bufGcd_dvd {ι : Type*} {S : Finset ι} {xi : ι → ℚ} {i : ι} (hi : i ∈ S) :
    bufGcd S xi ∣ carryNum (bufDen S xi) (xi i) := Finset.gcd_dvd hi

/-! ## D.36  The necessary lattice conditions -/

/-- **`bufDen_mul_mem_int`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  If the residual `e` is a signed subfamily sum
of the increments, then `D_buf · e` is an integer, namely the corresponding sum of the
`carryNum`s. -/
theorem bufDen_mul_mem_int {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {S T : Finset ι} {xi : ι → ℚ} {e : ℚ}
    (hTS : T ⊆ S) (he : e = ∑ i ∈ T, xi i) :
    ((bufDen S xi : ℚ)) * e = ((∑ i ∈ T, carryNum (bufDen S xi) (xi i) : ℤ) : ℚ) := by
  rw [he, Finset.mul_sum]
  push_cast
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i hi => ?_
  rw [carryNum_spec (den_dvd_bufDen (hTS hi))]

/-- **`absorber_lattice_necessary`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The exact lattice condition: the
integer `D_buf · e` is divisible by `b_buf`. -/
theorem absorber_lattice_necessary {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {S T : Finset ι} {xi : ι → ℚ}
    {e : ℚ} (hTS : T ⊆ S) (he : e = ∑ i ∈ T, xi i) :
    ∃ m : ℤ, ((bufDen S xi : ℚ)) * e = (m : ℚ) ∧ bufGcd S xi ∣ m := by
  refine ⟨∑ i ∈ T, carryNum (bufDen S xi) (xi i), bufDen_mul_mem_int hTS he, ?_⟩
  exact Finset.dvd_sum fun i hi => bufGcd_dvd (hTS hi)

/-! ## D.37  The exact signed absorber predicate — OPEN -/

/-- **Open node.**  An *exact signed absorber* for the residual `e`: a binary selection of at
most `bound` physically compatible protected switches whose signed increments sum to `e`
exactly.  This predicate is **not inhabited** anywhere in this project. -/
def ExactSignedAbsorber (a M : ℕ) (eps : ℕ → Bool) (e : ℚ) (S : Finset ℕ)
    (outSite innSite : ℕ → ℕ) (bound : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ T ⊆ S, T.card ≤ bound ∧
    (∑ i ∈ T, (1 / (innSite i : ℚ) - 1 / (outSite i : ℚ))) = e ∧
    (∀ i ∈ T, ProtectedSwitch a M eps (outSite i) (innSite i))

/-- **`exactSignedAbsorber_lattice_necessary`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Any exact signed absorber
satisfies the two lattice conditions, so the conditions are genuine obstructions to inhabiting
the predicate. -/
theorem exactSignedAbsorber_lattice_necessary {a M : ℕ} {eps : ℕ → Bool} {e : ℚ} {S : Finset ℕ}
    {outSite innSite : ℕ → ℕ} {bound : ℕ}
    (h : ExactSignedAbsorber a M eps e S outSite innSite bound) :
    ∃ m : ℤ,
      ((bufDen S (fun i => 1 / (innSite i : ℚ) - 1 / (outSite i : ℚ)) : ℚ)) * e = (m : ℚ) ∧
        bufGcd S (fun i => 1 / (innSite i : ℚ) - 1 / (outSite i : ℚ)) ∣ m := by
  obtain ⟨T, hTS, -, hsum, -⟩ := h
  exact absorber_lattice_necessary hTS hsum.symm

/-- **`absorber_switches_shift_value`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  A one-element absorber does move
the reciprocal value by exactly its increment, so the predicate has the intended meaning. -/
theorem absorber_switches_shift_value {a M : ℕ} {eps : ℕ → Bool} {out inn : ℕ}
    (hs : ProtectedSwitch a M eps out inn) :
    recipSum (selected a M (toggle eps out inn)) - recipSum (selected a M eps)
      = 1 / (inn : ℚ) - 1 / (out : ℚ) := by
  rw [recipSum_toggle hs]
  ring

end Direct
end Erdos287

@@END_FILE@@
@@BEGIN_FILE bytes=7099 sha256=1d8c627a32938d5328fbd648dd07f9d89fb6d20efcc724ee6be1d98a9f3af1b0 path=LEAN_PROJECT/RequestProject/Erdos287/Direct/BoundaryKernel.lean@@
import RequestProject.Erdos287.Direct.Core
import RequestProject.Erdos287.TopLayer

/-!
# Route D — the finite boundary-kernel API

INTERNAL #287 RESEARCH PROGRAMME ONLY.  **Erdős #287 is `OPEN` here and is not claimed.**

The boundary kernel is the finite high-valuation part of a hypothetical selection.  It is kept
strictly separated into

* **kernel variables** (the positions the kernel controls);
* **forced-zero pins** (positions that must be omitted);
* **forced-positive pins** (positions that must be selected);
* **feasibility** (existence of a mask obeying the pins and the local no-two-omissions rule);
* **top prime-power congruences** (imported from the elementary package, as a proved bridge).

The deterministic part — necessary conditions on the pins, the forced neighbours of a pinned
omission, and the *restriction* half of the extension/restriction bridge — is kernel-proved
here.  The *extension* half is genuinely an asymptotic/analytic statement and is therefore kept
as an explicit named interface proposition (`KernelExtensionInterface`), consumed by a
conditional bridge and never asserted.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace Erdos287
namespace Direct

/-! ## D.25  Kernel data and feasibility -/

/-- Finite boundary-kernel data on the ambient interval `[a, M]`. -/
structure KernelData where
  /-- the positions the kernel controls -/
  vars : Finset ℕ
  /-- positions pinned to be omitted -/
  forcedZero : Finset ℕ
  /-- positions pinned to be selected -/
  forcedOne : Finset ℕ

/-- A mask realises the kernel data. -/
def Realises (K : KernelData) (a M : ℕ) (eps : ℕ → Bool) : Prop :=
  (∀ n ∈ K.forcedZero, eps n = false) ∧ (∀ n ∈ K.forcedOne, eps n = true) ∧
    NoTwoConsecutiveOmissions a M eps

/-- The kernel data is feasible on `[a, M]`. -/
def Feasible (K : KernelData) (a M : ℕ) : Prop := ∃ eps : ℕ → Bool, Realises K a M eps

/-- **`feasible_pins_disjoint`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  A feasible kernel cannot pin a position
both ways. -/
theorem feasible_pins_disjoint {K : KernelData} {a M : ℕ} (h : Feasible K a M) :
    Disjoint K.forcedZero K.forcedOne := by
  obtain ⟨eps, hz, ho, -⟩ := h
  rw [Finset.disjoint_left]
  intro n hn hn'
  have := hz n hn
  rw [ho n hn'] at this
  exact absurd this (by simp)

/-- **`feasible_forcedZero_nonadjacent`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  A feasible kernel never pins two
adjacent positions of the window to zero. -/
theorem feasible_forcedZero_nonadjacent {K : KernelData} {a M : ℕ} (h : Feasible K a M)
    {n : ℕ} (hlo : a ≤ n) (hhi : n + 1 ≤ M)
    (h1 : n ∈ K.forcedZero) (h2 : n + 1 ∈ K.forcedZero) : False := by
  obtain ⟨eps, hz, -, hiso⟩ := h
  rcases hiso n hlo hhi with hc | hc
  · rw [hz n h1] at hc; exact absurd hc (by simp)
  · rw [hz (n + 1) h2] at hc; exact absurd hc (by simp)

/-- **`feasible_forces_neighbours`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Every realisation of a kernel with an
interior forced-zero pin selects both neighbours: the pins propagate deterministically. -/
theorem feasible_forces_neighbours {K : KernelData} {a M : ℕ} {eps : ℕ → Bool}
    (h : Realises K a M eps) {n : ℕ} (hlo : a < n) (hhi : n < M) (hn : n ∈ K.forcedZero) :
    eps (n - 1) = true ∧ eps (n + 1) = true :=
  neighbours_selected_of_omitted h.2.2 hlo hhi (h.1 n hn)

/-! ## D.26  Restriction (deterministic) and extension (interface) -/

/-- **`realises_restrict`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Restriction is deterministic: a realisation on
a window restricts to any subwindow, after restricting the pins. -/
theorem realises_restrict {K : KernelData} {a M a' M' : ℕ} {eps : ℕ → Bool}
    (h : Realises K a M eps) (h1 : a ≤ a') (h2 : M' ≤ M) :
    Realises { vars := K.vars.filter (fun n => a' ≤ n ∧ n ≤ M'),
               forcedZero := K.forcedZero.filter (fun n => a' ≤ n ∧ n ≤ M'),
               forcedOne := K.forcedOne.filter (fun n => a' ≤ n ∧ n ≤ M') } a' M' eps := by
  refine ⟨fun n hn => h.1 n (Finset.mem_of_mem_filter _ hn),
    fun n hn => h.2.1 n (Finset.mem_of_mem_filter _ hn), ?_⟩
  intro n hlo hhi
  exact h.2.2 n (le_trans h1 hlo) (le_trans hhi h2)

/-- **`feasible_restrict`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Feasibility is inherited by subwindows. -/
theorem feasible_restrict {K : KernelData} {a M a' M' : ℕ} (h : Feasible K a M)
    (h1 : a ≤ a') (h2 : M' ≤ M) :
    Feasible { vars := K.vars.filter (fun n => a' ≤ n ∧ n ≤ M'),
               forcedZero := K.forcedZero.filter (fun n => a' ≤ n ∧ n ≤ M'),
               forcedOne := K.forcedOne.filter (fun n => a' ≤ n ∧ n ≤ M') } a' M' := by
  obtain ⟨eps, heps⟩ := h
  exact ⟨eps, realises_restrict heps h1 h2⟩

/-- **Interface (open).**  Extension of a feasible boundary kernel to a *completed* selection
with prescribed reciprocal value.  This is the asymptotic/analytic half of the kernel bridge:
it is a named hypothesis, never an axiom, and it is **not** inhabited anywhere. -/
def KernelExtensionInterface (K : KernelData) (a M : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ eps : ℕ → Bool, Realises K a M eps →
    ∃ eps' : ℕ → Bool, Realises K a M eps' ∧ EndpointSelected a M eps' ∧
      recipSum (selected a M eps') = 1

/-- **`directCounterexample_of_kernelExtension`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED` bridge, `CONDITIONAL` on
the extension interface: a feasible kernel plus the interface produces a Route-D
counterexample.  Nothing here proves the interface. -/
theorem directCounterexample_of_kernelExtension {K : KernelData} {a M : ℕ}
    (ha : 1 < a) (haM : a < M) (hfeas : Feasible K a M)
    (hext : KernelExtensionInterface K a M) :
    ∃ eps : ℕ → Bool, DirectCounterexample a M eps := by
  obtain ⟨eps, heps⟩ := hfeas
  obtain ⟨eps', hreal, hend, hsum⟩ := hext eps heps
  exact ⟨eps', ⟨ha, haM, hend, hreal.2.2, hsum⟩⟩

/-! ## D.27  Top prime-power congruences of the selected set

These are *proved* consequences of the elementary package, imported into Route D as bridges. -/

/-- **`direct_topLayer_congruence`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED` bridge.  The top `p`-adic layer of the
selected set of a Route-D counterexample satisfies the cofactor congruence. -/
theorem direct_topLayer_congruence {a M : ℕ} {eps : ℕ → Bool} (h : DirectCounterexample a M eps)
    {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (he : 1 ≤ topExp (selected a M eps) p) :
    (∑ x ∈ topLayer (selected a M eps) p, (((ordCompl[p] x : ℕ) : ZMod p))⁻¹) = 0 := by
  refine topLayer_congruence (selected a M eps) p hp ?_ h.sum_one he
  intro n hn
  have hlo := (mem_selected.1 hn).1.1
  have ha := h.one_lt
  omega

/-- **`direct_topLayer_card_ne_one`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED` bridge.  The top layer of a Route-D
counterexample is never a singleton. -/
theorem direct_topLayer_card_ne_one {a M : ℕ} {eps : ℕ → Bool} (h : DirectCounterexample a M eps)
    {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (he : 1 ≤ topExp (selected a M eps) p) :
    (topLayer (selected a M eps) p).card ≠ 1 := by
  refine topLayer_card_ne_one (selected a M eps) p hp ?_ h.sum_one he
  intro n hn
  have hlo := (mem_selected.1 hn).1.1
  have ha := h.one_lt
  omega

end Direct
end Erdos287

@@END_FILE@@
@@BEGIN_FILE bytes=8349 sha256=c2cb08b60aaf4a0dea038a8c3be2d2464b3f0126f44544bc77e61a4f2a2ffde4 path=LEAN_PROJECT/RequestProject/Erdos287/Direct/Core.lean@@
import Mathlib
import RequestProject.Erdos287.ProblemStatement

/-!
# Erdős #287 — Route D (Direct Reciprocal programme), core definitions

INTERNAL #287 RESEARCH PROGRAMME ONLY.  **Erdős #287 is `OPEN` here and is not claimed.**

This namespace (`Erdos287.Direct`) is a *new, append-only* development.  It is a second,
alternative proof route ("Route D"), and it is deliberately kept disjoint from the existing
Source / FivePrime / Directed-Selberg / Physical-`k=1` programme ("Route S").  No node of
one route discharges a node of the other unless an explicit bridge theorem is proved; see
`Direct/Reconciliation.lean`.

This file fixes the combinatorial source of Route D:

* the ambient interval `I = [a, M]` and a Boolean selection `eps`;
* the selected set `A = selected a M eps` and its reciprocal sum;
* the endpoint-selected predicate and the no-two-consecutive-omissions predicate;
* the exact Route-D counterexample predicate `DirectCounterexample`;
* the two bridges to the project's exact predicate `Erdos287Counterexample`, proved in both
  directions (no equivalence is asserted by comment only).

All conventions are explicit: positions are natural numbers, reciprocal sums are rational.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace Erdos287
namespace Direct

/-! ## D.1  The ambient interval, the selection and the selected set -/

/-- The ambient interval `I = [a, M]` of Route D. -/
def ambient (a M : ℕ) : Finset ℕ := Finset.Icc a M

/-- The set selected by the Boolean mask `eps` inside `[a, M]`. -/
def selected (a M : ℕ) (eps : ℕ → Bool) : Finset ℕ :=
  (ambient a M).filter (fun n => eps n = true)

@[simp] theorem mem_selected {a M : ℕ} {eps : ℕ → Bool} {n : ℕ} :
    n ∈ selected a M eps ↔ (a ≤ n ∧ n ≤ M) ∧ eps n = true := by
  simp [selected, ambient, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_Icc, and_assoc]

theorem selected_subset_ambient (a M : ℕ) (eps : ℕ → Bool) :
    selected a M eps ⊆ ambient a M := Finset.filter_subset _ _

/-- The reciprocal sum of a finite set of positions. -/
def recipSum (A : Finset ℕ) : ℚ := ∑ n ∈ A, (1 : ℚ) / n

@[simp] theorem recipSum_empty : recipSum ∅ = 0 := by simp [recipSum]

theorem recipSum_insert {A : Finset ℕ} {n : ℕ} (h : n ∉ A) :
    recipSum (insert n A) = (1 : ℚ) / n + recipSum A := by
  simp [recipSum, Finset.sum_insert h]

/-! ## D.2  The two structural predicates -/

/-- Both endpoints of the ambient interval are selected. -/
def EndpointSelected (a M : ℕ) (eps : ℕ → Bool) : Prop := eps a = true ∧ eps M = true

/-- No two consecutive positions of `[a, M]` are simultaneously omitted. -/
def NoTwoConsecutiveOmissions (a M : ℕ) (eps : ℕ → Bool) : Prop :=
  ∀ n : ℕ, a ≤ n → n + 1 ≤ M → eps n = true ∨ eps (n + 1) = true

/-- **The exact Route-D counterexample predicate.** -/
structure DirectCounterexample (a M : ℕ) (eps : ℕ → Bool) : Prop where
  /-- the least position exceeds `1` -/
  one_lt : 1 < a
  /-- the interval is nondegenerate -/
  lt : a < M
  /-- both endpoints are selected -/
  endpoints : EndpointSelected a M eps
  /-- omissions are isolated -/
  isolated : NoTwoConsecutiveOmissions a M eps
  /-- the selected reciprocals sum to `1` -/
  sum_one : recipSum (selected a M eps) = 1

/-! ## D.3  Elementary consequences of the two structural predicates -/

theorem left_mem_selected {a M : ℕ} {eps : ℕ → Bool} (hle : a ≤ M)
    (h : EndpointSelected a M eps) : a ∈ selected a M eps := by
  simp [mem_selected, hle, h.1]

theorem right_mem_selected {a M : ℕ} {eps : ℕ → Bool} (hle : a ≤ M)
    (h : EndpointSelected a M eps) : M ∈ selected a M eps := by
  simp [mem_selected, hle, h.2]

/-- An omitted position strictly inside the interval has both neighbours selected. -/
theorem neighbours_selected_of_omitted {a M : ℕ} {eps : ℕ → Bool}
    (hiso : NoTwoConsecutiveOmissions a M eps) {n : ℕ}
    (hlo : a < n) (hhi : n < M) (hn : eps n = false) :
    eps (n - 1) = true ∧ eps (n + 1) = true := by
  constructor
  · have := hiso (n - 1) (by omega) (by omega)
    rcases this with h | h
    · exact h
    · rw [show n - 1 + 1 = n by omega] at h; rw [hn] at h; exact absurd h (by simp)
  · have := hiso n (by omega) (by omega)
    rcases this with h | h
    · rw [hn] at h; exact absurd h (by simp)
    · exact h

/-- Every gap of the selected set is at most `2`. -/
theorem gap_le_two_of_isolated {a M : ℕ} {eps : ℕ → Bool}
    (hend : EndpointSelected a M eps) (hiso : NoTwoConsecutiveOmissions a M eps)
    {n : ℕ} (hn : n ∈ selected a M eps) (hlt : n < M) :
    n + 1 ∈ selected a M eps ∨ n + 2 ∈ selected a M eps := by
  rw [mem_selected] at hn
  obtain ⟨⟨hna, hnM⟩, _⟩ := hn
  by_cases hM : n + 1 = M
  · left; rw [mem_selected]; exact ⟨⟨by omega, by omega⟩, by rw [hM]; exact hend.2⟩
  · have h := hiso (n + 1) (by omega) (by omega)
    rcases h with h | h
    · left; exact mem_selected.2 ⟨⟨by omega, by omega⟩, h⟩
    · right; exact mem_selected.2 ⟨⟨by omega, by omega⟩, by simpa [Nat.add_assoc] using h⟩

/-! ## D.4  Bridges to the project's exact `Erdos287Counterexample` predicate

These are proved, not asserted.  The forward bridge shows Route D's source really is a
source of counterexamples to #287; the backward bridge shows nothing is lost by working
with masks. -/

/-- **`directCounterexample_to_exact`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  A Route-D counterexample yields
an exact `Erdos287Counterexample`. -/
theorem directCounterexample_to_exact {a M : ℕ} {eps : ℕ → Bool}
    (h : DirectCounterexample a M eps) : Erdos287Counterexample (selected a M eps) := by
  have hle : a ≤ M := le_of_lt h.lt
  have ha : a ∈ selected a M eps := left_mem_selected hle h.endpoints
  have hM : M ∈ selected a M eps := right_mem_selected hle h.endpoints
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, h.sum_one, ?_⟩
  · have hsub : ({a, M} : Finset ℕ) ⊆ selected a M eps := by
      intro x hx
      rcases Finset.mem_insert.1 hx with rfl | hx
      · exact ha
      · rw [Finset.mem_singleton] at hx; subst hx; exact hM
    have hcard : ({a, M} : Finset ℕ).card = 2 := by
      rw [Finset.card_insert_of_notMem (by simp [Nat.ne_of_lt h.lt]), Finset.card_singleton]
    calc (2 : ℕ) = ({a, M} : Finset ℕ).card := hcard.symm
      _ ≤ (selected a M eps).card := Finset.card_le_card hsub
  · intro x hx
    rw [mem_selected] at hx
    exact lt_of_lt_of_le h.one_lt hx.1.1
  · intro x hx hex
    obtain ⟨b, hb, hxb⟩ := hex
    have hbM : b ≤ M := (mem_selected.1 hb).1.2
    exact gap_le_two_of_isolated h.endpoints h.isolated hx (by omega)

/-- **`exact_to_directCounterexample`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Conversely, every exact
`Erdos287Counterexample` is the selected set of a Route-D counterexample on its own
min/max window, with `eps` the membership mask. -/
theorem exact_to_directCounterexample {A : Finset ℕ} (h : Erdos287Counterexample A) :
    DirectCounterexample (A.min' h.nonempty) (A.max' h.nonempty)
      (fun n => decide (n ∈ A)) ∧
      selected (A.min' h.nonempty) (A.max' h.nonempty) (fun n => decide (n ∈ A)) = A := by
  set N := A.min' h.nonempty with hN
  set M := A.max' h.nonempty with hMdef
  have hNmem : N ∈ A := Finset.min'_mem _ _
  have hMmem : M ∈ A := Finset.max'_mem _ _
  have hsel : selected N M (fun n => decide (n ∈ A)) = A := by
    ext x
    simp only [mem_selected, decide_eq_true_eq]
    constructor
    · exact fun hx => hx.2
    · intro hx
      exact ⟨⟨Finset.min'_le _ _ hx, Finset.le_max' _ _ hx⟩, hx⟩
  have hNM : N < M := by
    rcases lt_trichotomy N M with hlt | heq | hgt
    · exact hlt
    · exfalso
      have hcard := h.card_ge
      have : A ⊆ {N} := by
        intro x hx
        have h1 : N ≤ x := Finset.min'_le _ _ hx
        have h2 : x ≤ M := Finset.le_max' _ _ hx
        rw [← heq] at h2
        simp [Finset.mem_singleton]; omega
      have := Finset.card_le_card this
      simp at this; omega
    · exact absurd (Finset.min'_le _ _ hMmem) (by omega)
  refine ⟨⟨h.one_lt N hNmem, hNM, ⟨by simpa using hNmem, by simpa using hMmem⟩, ?_, ?_⟩, hsel⟩
  · intro n hn hn'
    have := (h.toGap2CE).holes_isolated n (by simpa [Gap2CE.N, hN] using hn)
      (by simpa [Gap2CE.M, hMdef] using hn')
    simpa using this
  · rw [hsel]; exact h.sum_one

end Direct
end Erdos287

import RequestProject.Erdos287.Direct.BoundaryKernel
import RequestProject.Erdos287.Direct.SparseSubreservoir
import RequestProject.Erdos287.Direct.AbsorberInterfaces
import RequestProject.Erdos287.Direct.LCMCarry

/-!
# Route D — current formal status ledger

INTERNAL #287 RESEARCH PROGRAMME ONLY.  **Erdős #287 is `OPEN` here and is not claimed.**

This is the Route-D ledger.  It is *separate* from the Route-S ledger
(`Erdos287.Effectivity.latestEvidence` and its cut set), which is untouched; the two are
reconciled — without merging — in `Direct/Reconciliation.lean`.

Evidence classes follow the required taxonomy.  A published analytic theorem is **never**
tagged `kernelProved` merely because a bridge consuming it is kernel-proved.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace Erdos287
namespace Direct

/-! ## D.38  Evidence taxonomy -/

/-- The evidence taxonomy of the Direct route. -/
inductive EvidenceDirect
  /-- reconstructed in the Lean kernel here, with no unproved hypothesis -/
  | kernelProved
  /-- kernel-proved *from explicitly named interface hypotheses* -/
  | kernelConditional
  /-- an external published theorem, not formalised here -/
  | externalPublished
  /-- an external claim with no published proof and no formalisation -/
  | externalUnformalised
  /-- awaiting a finite certificate that is not present in this repository -/
  | finiteCertificatePending
  /-- open -/
  | openNode
  /-- retired because refuted -/
  | retiredFalse
  /-- correct but cannot close its target -/
  | nonclosing
  /-- status not determined here -/
  | unknown
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Only kernel-proved content counts as closed. -/
def EvidenceDirect.isClosed : EvidenceDirect → Bool
  | .kernelProved => true
  | _ => false

/-! ## D.39  Nodes -/

/-- The Route-D nodes tracked at this checkpoint. -/
inductive DirectNode
  /-- the combinatorial source and its bridges to the exact #287 predicate -/
  | directCore
  /-- the exact ambient-LCM reciprocal compiler -/
  | reciprocalCompiler
  /-- deterministic raw-mask arithmetic -/
  | rawMaskArithmetic
  /-- exact mask counting (needs a prime-counting input) -/
  | maskCountIdentities
  /-- restriction half of the boundary-kernel bridge -/
  | kernelRestriction
  /-- extension half of the boundary-kernel bridge -/
  | kernelExtension
  /-- the finite Fourier all-target lemma -/
  | finiteFourierAllTarget
  /-- the reciprocal exponential-sum input -/
  | reciprocalExpSumInput
  /-- the sparse subreservoir claim -/
  | sparseSubreservoir
  /-- exact LCM / carry algebra -/
  | lcmCarryAlgebra
  /-- the exact path-polynomial target theorem -/
  | pathPolynomialTarget
  /-- the value-preserving switch -/
  | valuePreservingSwitch
  /-- the value-moving switch -/
  | valueMovingSwitch
  /-- analytic supply/abundance of switches -/
  | switchSupply
  /-- the deterministic target-tuning bridge -/
  | targetTuningBridge
  /-- the exact signed absorber -/
  | exactSignedAbsorber
  /-- classification of augmented-mask/kernel survivors -/
  | maskSurvivorClassification
  /-- the full exact assembly of Route D -/
  | fullAssembly
  /-- unrestricted Erdős #287 -/
  | erdos287
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Evidence class of each Route-D node. -/
def directEvidence : DirectNode → EvidenceDirect
  | .directCore => .kernelProved
  | .reciprocalCompiler => .kernelProved
  | .rawMaskArithmetic => .kernelProved
  | .maskCountIdentities => .kernelConditional
  | .kernelRestriction => .kernelProved
  | .kernelExtension => .openNode
  | .finiteFourierAllTarget => .kernelProved
  | .reciprocalExpSumInput => .externalPublished
  | .sparseSubreservoir => .openNode
  | .lcmCarryAlgebra => .kernelProved
  | .pathPolynomialTarget => .kernelProved
  | .valuePreservingSwitch => .kernelProved
  | .valueMovingSwitch => .kernelProved
  | .switchSupply => .openNode
  | .targetTuningBridge => .kernelConditional
  | .exactSignedAbsorber => .openNode
  | .maskSurvivorClassification => .openNode
  | .fullAssembly => .openNode
  | .erdos287 => .openNode

/-- **`direct_erdos287_open`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED` bookkeeping. -/
theorem direct_erdos287_open : directEvidence .erdos287 = EvidenceDirect.openNode := rfl

/-! ## D.40  What the closed nodes actually are

Each `kernelProved` tag below is discharged by exhibiting the theorem it refers to. -/

/-- **`directCore_closed`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The source bridges hold in both directions. -/
theorem directCore_closed :
    directEvidence .directCore = EvidenceDirect.kernelProved ∧
      (∀ (a M : ℕ) (eps : ℕ → Bool), DirectCounterexample a M eps →
        Erdos287Counterexample (selected a M eps)) ∧
      (∀ (A : Finset ℕ) (h : Erdos287Counterexample A),
        selected (A.min' h.nonempty) (A.max' h.nonempty) (fun n => decide (n ∈ A)) = A) :=
  ⟨rfl, fun _ _ _ h => directCounterexample_to_exact h,
    fun _ h => (exact_to_directCounterexample h).2⟩

/-- **`reciprocalCompiler_closed`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`. -/
theorem reciprocalCompiler_closed :
    directEvidence .reciprocalCompiler = EvidenceDirect.kernelProved ∧
      (∀ (I : Finset ℕ), 0 ∉ I → ∀ A ⊆ I,
        (recipSum A = 1 ↔ ∑ n ∈ A, setLcm I / n = setLcm I)) :=
  ⟨rfl, fun _ h0 _ hA => compiler_ambient h0 hA⟩

/-- **`rawMask_closed`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Uniqueness of the large-prime factorisation in the
established regime. -/
theorem rawMask_closed :
    directEvidence .rawMaskArithmetic = EvidenceDirect.kernelProved ∧
      (∀ (M : ℕ), 18632 ≤ M → ∀ n d₁ r₁ d₂ r₂ : ℕ, 0 < n →
        n = d₁ * r₁ → r₁.Prime → M < 137 * r₁ →
        n = d₂ * r₂ → r₂.Prime → M < 137 * r₂ → d₂ ≤ 136 → r₁ = r₂ ∧ d₁ = d₂) :=
  ⟨rfl, fun _ hM _ _ _ _ _ hn h₁ hp₁ hlt₁ h₂ hp₂ hlt₂ hd₂ =>
    largePrime_factorisation_unique hM hn h₁ hp₁ hlt₁ h₂ hp₂ hlt₂ hd₂⟩

/-- **`lcmCarry_closed`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The jump identity and the descending recurrence. -/
theorem lcmCarry_closed :
    directEvidence .lcmCarryAlgebra = EvidenceDirect.kernelProved ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → LN (n + 1) = JN (n + 1) * LN n) ∧
      (∀ p k : ℕ, p.Prime → 1 ≤ k → JN (p ^ k) = p) ∧
      (∀ N : ℕ, ¬ IsPrimePow N → JN N = 1) :=
  ⟨rfl, fun n hn => LN_succ_eq n hn, fun _ _ hp hk => JN_prime_pow hp hk,
    fun _ h => JN_of_not_isPrimePow h⟩

/-- **`pathPolynomial_closed`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The exact target theorem. -/
theorem pathPolynomial_closed :
    directEvidence .pathPolynomialTarget = EvidenceDirect.kernelProved ∧
      (∀ (P V : Finset ℕ) (ell τ : ℕ), ell ≠ 0 → Disjoint P V →
        (∀ n ∈ P, n ≠ 0 ∧ n ∣ ell) → (∀ n ∈ V, n ≠ 0 ∧ n ∣ ell) →
        (∑ n ∈ P, ell / n) + τ = ell →
        ((∃ J ∈ indepSubsets V, recipSum (P ∪ J) = 1) ↔
          0 < (pathPoly V (fun n => ell / n)).coeff τ)) :=
  ⟨rfl, fun _ _ _ _ hell hdisj hP hV hτ => exact_reciprocal_target hell hdisj hP hV hτ⟩

/-- **`finiteFourier_closed`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The finite all-target lemma is internal
finite mathematics: it is proved in the kernel, *not* assumed. -/
theorem finiteFourier_closed :
    directEvidence .finiteFourierAllTarget = EvidenceDirect.kernelProved ∧
      (∀ (q : ℕ) (_ : NeZero q) (C : Finset ℕ) (a : ℕ → ZMod q) (B : ℝ),
        (∀ ψ : AddChar (ZMod q) ℂ, ψ ≠ 0 → ‖∏ n ∈ C, (1 + ψ (a n))‖ ≤ B) →
        ((q : ℝ) - 1) * B < 2 ^ C.card → ∀ t : ZMod q, 0 < subsetSumCount q C a t) :=
  ⟨rfl, fun _ _ C a B hB hlt t => subsetSumCount_pos_of_bound C a B hB hlt t⟩

/-- **`switches_closed`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Both switch calculi. -/
theorem switches_closed :
    directEvidence .valuePreservingSwitch = EvidenceDirect.kernelProved ∧
      directEvidence .valueMovingSwitch = EvidenceDirect.kernelProved ∧
      (∀ k : ℚ, k ≠ 0 → 1 / (6 * k) = 1 / (10 * k) + 1 / (15 * k)) ∧
      (∀ a M : ℕ, ∀ eps : ℕ → Bool, ∀ out inn : ℕ, ProtectedSwitch a M eps out inn →
        recipSum (selected a M (toggle eps out inn)) =
          recipSum (selected a M eps) + 1 / (inn : ℚ) - 1 / (out : ℚ)) :=
  ⟨rfl, rfl, fun k hk => sixSwitch_identity k hk, fun _ _ _ _ _ hs => recipSum_toggle hs⟩

/-! ## D.41  The conditional nodes -/

/-- **`targetTuning_is_conditional`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED` bookkeeping.  The tuning bridge is
tagged `kernelConditional`, never `kernelProved`: it is proved only from its four named
interfaces. -/
theorem targetTuning_is_conditional :
    directEvidence .targetTuningBridge = EvidenceDirect.kernelConditional ∧
      (∀ (a M K : ℕ) (ch : ℕ → (ℕ → Bool)) (E : ℚ) (budget : ℕ), 0 ≤ E →
        CoarseSwitchSupply a M K ch → FineSwitchSupply a M K ch E →
        HarmonicInterior a M K ch → SparseRepairCost a M K ch budget →
        TargetStraddling a M E budget) :=
  ⟨rfl, fun _ _ _ _ _ _ hE h1 h2 h3 h4 => targetTuning_of hE h1 h2 h3 h4⟩

/-- **`expSumInput_is_external`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED` bookkeeping.  The reciprocal
exponential-sum bound is an external published input: it is tagged `externalPublished`, is
*not* closed, and appears only as a hypothesis. -/
theorem expSumInput_is_external :
    directEvidence .reciprocalExpSumInput = EvidenceDirect.externalPublished ∧
      (directEvidence .reciprocalExpSumInput).isClosed = false ∧
      (∀ (q : ℕ) (_ : NeZero q) (C : Finset ℕ) (B : ℝ), ReciprocalExpSumInterface q C B →
        ((q : ℝ) - 1) * B < 2 ^ C.card → AttainsAllTargets q C) :=
  ⟨rfl, rfl, fun _ _ _ _ hBG hlt => allTargets_of_expSumInterface hBG hlt⟩

/-- **`absorber_open`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED` bookkeeping.  The exact signed absorber is open: only
its necessary lattice conditions are proved, and the predicate is not inhabited. -/
theorem absorber_open :
    directEvidence .exactSignedAbsorber = EvidenceDirect.openNode ∧
      (∀ (a M : ℕ) (eps : ℕ → Bool) (e : ℚ) (S : Finset ℕ) (outSite innSite : ℕ → ℕ)
        (bound : ℕ), ExactSignedAbsorber a M eps e S outSite innSite bound →
        ∃ m : ℤ,
          ((bufDen S (fun i => 1 / (innSite i : ℚ) - 1 / (outSite i : ℚ)) : ℚ)) * e = (m : ℚ) ∧
            bufGcd S (fun i => 1 / (innSite i : ℚ) - 1 / (outSite i : ℚ)) ∣ m) :=
  ⟨rfl, fun _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ h => exactSignedAbsorber_lattice_necessary h⟩

/-! ## D.42  Dependencies and the current Route-D cut -/

/-- Recorded prerequisites of the Route-D nodes. -/
def directDeps : DirectNode → List DirectNode
  | .maskSurvivorClassification => [.rawMaskArithmetic, .kernelRestriction, .lcmCarryAlgebra]
  | .kernelExtension => [.kernelRestriction]
  | .sparseSubreservoir => [.finiteFourierAllTarget, .reciprocalExpSumInput]
  | .targetTuningBridge => [.valueMovingSwitch, .valuePreservingSwitch]
  | .exactSignedAbsorber => [.valueMovingSwitch]
  | .fullAssembly =>
      [.directCore, .reciprocalCompiler, .pathPolynomialTarget, .maskSurvivorClassification,
        .switchSupply, .exactSignedAbsorber, .kernelExtension, .sparseSubreservoir]
  | .erdos287 => [.fullAssembly]
  | _ => []

/-- The current Route-D conceptual cut: `D1` survivors, `D2` analytic activation/supply,
`D3` exact absorber, `D4` full assembly. -/
def directCutSet : List DirectNode :=
  [.maskSurvivorClassification, .switchSupply, .kernelExtension, .sparseSubreservoir,
    .exactSignedAbsorber, .fullAssembly]

/-- **`directCut_all_open`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Every Route-D cut node is open. -/
theorem directCut_all_open : ∀ n ∈ directCutSet, directEvidence n = EvidenceDirect.openNode := by
  intro n hn
  fin_cases hn <;> rfl

/-- **`directCut_not_closed`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  No cut node is tagged closed. -/
theorem directCut_not_closed : ∀ n ∈ directCutSet, (directEvidence n).isClosed = false := by
  intro n hn
  fin_cases hn <;> rfl

/-- The independence of the four conceptual Route-D cut nodes has **not** been established by
dependency analysis; it is recorded as `unknown`, not asserted. -/
def directCutIndependence : EvidenceDirect := .unknown

/-- **`directCut_independence_unknown`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED` bookkeeping.  In particular the
recorded dependency graph does *not* make the cut nodes pairwise independent: `fullAssembly`
depends on four of them. -/
theorem directCut_independence_unknown :
    directCutIndependence = EvidenceDirect.unknown ∧
      DirectNode.maskSurvivorClassification ∈ directDeps .fullAssembly ∧
      DirectNode.switchSupply ∈ directDeps .fullAssembly ∧
      DirectNode.exactSignedAbsorber ∈ directDeps .fullAssembly ∧
      DirectNode.kernelExtension ∈ directDeps .fullAssembly := by
  refine ⟨rfl, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩ <;> simp [directDeps]

/-- **`erdos287_needs_directCut`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Erdős #287 depends, along Route D, on
the full assembly, which depends on the whole cut. -/
theorem erdos287_needs_directCut :
    directDeps .erdos287 = [DirectNode.fullAssembly] ∧
      (∀ n ∈ directCutSet, n = DirectNode.fullAssembly ∨ n ∈ directDeps .fullAssembly) := by
  refine ⟨rfl, ?_⟩
  intro n hn
  fin_cases hn <;> simp [directDeps]

end Direct

import RequestProject.Erdos287.Direct.RawMask

/-!
# Route D — exact LCM / cofactor-carry algebra

INTERNAL #287 RESEARCH PROGRAMME ONLY.  **Erdős #287 is `OPEN` here and is not claimed.**

This module formalises the exact arithmetic of the running denominators:

* `LN N = lcm(1, …, N)` and the exact prime-power divisibility criterion
  `p^e ∣ LN N ↔ p^e ≤ N` (`prime_pow_dvd_LN`);
* the jump `J_N = L_N / L_{N-1}`, proved to be `p` when `N = p^r` is a prime power and `1`
  otherwise (`LN_succ_eq`, `JN_prime_pow`, `JN_of_not_isPrimePow`, `JN_eq_div`);
* the exact layer quotients `T_q ↦ C_q` (valid exactly when `q ∣ T_q`) and the fibrewise
  aggregation `C_N = ∑_{⌊M/q⌋ = N} C_q`, proved as an exact partition identity
  (`carry_aggregate`);
* the descending exact recurrence `z_{N-1} = (z_N − C_N)/J_N` together with its exact
  divisibility side condition (`descending_recurrence`, `descending_step_iff`).

**No complexity claim is made.**  The recurrence is an exact identity; nothing here states
or implies that evaluating it is a polynomial-time algorithm.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace Erdos287
namespace Direct

/-! ## D.13  `L_N = lcm(1, …, N)` -/

/-- `LN N = lcm(1, 2, …, N)`, with `LN 0 = 1`. -/
def LN : ℕ → ℕ
  | 0 => 1
  | (n + 1) => Nat.lcm (LN n) (n + 1)

@[simp] theorem LN_zero : LN 0 = 1 := rfl

theorem LN_succ (n : ℕ) : LN (n + 1) = Nat.lcm (LN n) (n + 1) := rfl

theorem LN_ne_zero : ∀ n : ℕ, LN n ≠ 0
  | 0 => by simp
  | (n + 1) => by
      rw [LN_succ]
      exact Nat.lcm_ne_zero (LN_ne_zero n) (Nat.succ_ne_zero n)

theorem LN_pos (n : ℕ) : 0 < LN n := Nat.pos_of_ne_zero (LN_ne_zero n)

theorem LN_dvd_succ (n : ℕ) : LN n ∣ LN (n + 1) := by
  rw [LN_succ]; exact Nat.dvd_lcm_left _ _

/-- Every positive `k ≤ N` divides `L_N`. -/
theorem dvd_LN {k N : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k) (h : k ≤ N) : k ∣ LN N := by
  induction N with
  | zero => omega
  | succ n ih =>
      rcases Nat.lt_or_ge k (n + 1) with hlt | hge
      · exact dvd_trans (ih (by omega)) (LN_dvd_succ n)
      · have hkn : k = n + 1 := by omega
        subst hkn
        rw [LN_succ]; exact Nat.dvd_lcm_right _ _

/-- **`prime_pow_dvd_LN`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  For a prime `p` and `e ≥ 1`,
`p^e ∣ lcm(1,…,N)` holds exactly when `p^e ≤ N`. -/
theorem prime_pow_dvd_LN {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) {e : ℕ} (he : 1 ≤ e) :
    ∀ N : ℕ, (p ^ e ∣ LN N ↔ p ^ e ≤ N) := by
  intro N
  induction N with
  | zero =>
      simp only [LN_zero, Nat.le_zero]
      have hpe : 1 < p ^ e := Nat.one_lt_pow (by omega) hp.one_lt
      constructor
      · intro h
        have := Nat.le_of_dvd one_pos h
        omega
      · intro h; omega
  | succ n ih =>
      rw [LN_succ]
      constructor
      · intro h
        have hLN : LN n ≠ 0 := LN_ne_zero n
        have hn1 : (n + 1 : ℕ) ≠ 0 := Nat.succ_ne_zero n
        have hlcm0 : Nat.lcm (LN n) (n + 1) ≠ 0 := Nat.lcm_ne_zero hLN hn1
        rw [Nat.Prime.pow_dvd_iff_le_factorization hp hlcm0,
          Nat.factorization_lcm hLN hn1] at h
        simp only [Finsupp.sup_apply, le_sup_iff] at h
        rcases h with h | h
        · rw [← Nat.Prime.pow_dvd_iff_le_factorization hp hLN] at h
          exact le_trans (ih.1 h) (by omega)
        · rw [← Nat.Prime.pow_dvd_iff_le_factorization hp hn1] at h
          exact Nat.le_of_dvd (by omega) h
      · intro h
        rcases Nat.lt_or_ge (p ^ e) (n + 1) with hlt | hge
        · exact dvd_trans (ih.2 (by omega)) (Nat.dvd_lcm_left _ _)
        · have hpe : p ^ e = n + 1 := by omega
          rw [hpe]
          exact Nat.dvd_lcm_right _ _

/-! ## D.14  The jump `J_N = L_N / L_{N-1}` -/

open Classical in
/-- The jump factor `J_N`: the prime `p` if `N = p^r` is a prime power, and `1` otherwise. -/
noncomputable def JN (N : ℕ) : ℕ := if IsPrimePow N then N.minFac else 1

theorem JN_of_not_isPrimePow {N : ℕ} (h : ¬ IsPrimePow N) : JN N = 1 := by
  rw [JN, if_neg h]

/-- **`JN_prime_pow`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  `J_{p^k} = p` for a prime `p` and `k ≥ 1`. -/
theorem JN_prime_pow {p k : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hk : 1 ≤ k) : JN (p ^ k) = p := by
  have hpp : IsPrimePow (p ^ k) := (isPrimePow_nat_iff _).2 ⟨p, k, hp, by omega, rfl⟩
  rw [JN, if_pos hpp, hp.pow_minFac (by omega)]

/-- **`LN_succ_eq`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The exact one-step growth of `lcm(1,…,N)`:
`L_N = J_N · L_{N-1}`. -/
theorem LN_succ_eq (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) : LN (n + 1) = JN (n + 1) * LN n := by
  by_cases hpp : IsPrimePow (n + 1)
  · obtain ⟨p, k, hp, hk, hpk⟩ := (isPrimePow_nat_iff (n + 1)).1 hpp
    have hJ : JN (n + 1) = p := by rw [← hpk, JN_prime_pow hp (by omega)]
    -- `p^(k-1) ∣ L_n`, because `p^(k-1) ≤ n`
    have hlt : p ^ (k - 1) < p ^ k := Nat.pow_lt_pow_right hp.one_lt (by omega)
    have hle : p ^ (k - 1) ≤ n := by omega
    have hdvd1 : p ^ (k - 1) ∣ LN n := by
      rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos (k - 1) with h0 | h0
      · rw [h0]; simp
      · exact (prime_pow_dvd_LN hp h0 n).2 hle
    -- the gcd is exactly `p^(k-1)`
    have hgcd : Nat.gcd (LN n) (p ^ k) = p ^ (k - 1) := by
      obtain ⟨j, hjk, hj⟩ := (Nat.dvd_prime_pow hp).1 (Nat.gcd_dvd_right (LN n) (p ^ k))
      have hjdvd : p ^ j ∣ LN n := hj ▸ Nat.gcd_dvd_left (LN n) (p ^ k)
      have hjle : j ≤ k - 1 := by
        rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos j with rfl | hj0
        · omega
        · have hjn : p ^ j ≤ n := (prime_pow_dvd_LN hp hj0 n).1 hjdvd
          by_contra hcon
          have : p ^ k ≤ p ^ j := Nat.pow_le_pow_right hp.one_le (by omega)
          omega
      have hge : p ^ (k - 1) ∣ p ^ j := hj ▸ Nat.dvd_gcd hdvd1 (pow_dvd_pow p (by omega))
      have : k - 1 ≤ j := (Nat.pow_dvd_pow_iff_le_right hp.one_lt).1 hge
      rw [hj]
      congr 1
      omega
    have hmul := Nat.gcd_mul_lcm (LN n) (p ^ k)
    rw [hgcd] at hmul
    have hsplit : p ^ k = p ^ (k - 1) * p := by
      rw [← pow_succ]
      congr 1
      omega
    have hcancel : p ^ (k - 1) * Nat.lcm (LN n) (p ^ k) = p ^ (k - 1) * (p * LN n) := by
      rw [hmul, hsplit]; ring
    have hppos : 0 < p ^ (k - 1) := Nat.pow_pos hp.pos
    have hlcm : Nat.lcm (LN n) (p ^ k) = p * LN n :=
      Nat.eq_of_mul_eq_mul_left hppos hcancel
    rw [LN_succ, hJ, ← hpk, hlcm]
  · -- not a prime power: `n+1` divides `L_n`, so the LCM does not grow
    have hN2 : 2 ≤ n + 1 := by omega
    have hN0 : (n + 1 : ℕ) ≠ 0 := by omega
    have hN1 : (n + 1 : ℕ) ≠ 1 := by omega
    set p := (n + 1).minFac with hpdef
    have hp : p.Prime := Nat.minFac_prime hN1
    have hpdvd : p ∣ n + 1 := Nat.minFac_dvd _
    set k := (n + 1).factorization p with hkdef
    have hk : 0 < k := hp.factorization_pos_of_dvd hN0 hpdvd
    set b := (n + 1) / p ^ k with hbdef
    have hab : p ^ k * b = n + 1 := Nat.ordProj_mul_ordCompl_eq_self (n + 1) p
    have hcop : Nat.Coprime (p ^ k) b := (Nat.coprime_ordCompl hp hN0).pow_left k
    have hb1 : b ≠ 1 := by
      intro hb
      rw [hb, mul_one] at hab
      exact hpp ((isPrimePow_nat_iff _).2 ⟨p, k, hp, hk, hab⟩)
    have hb0 : b ≠ 0 := by
      intro hb; rw [hb, mul_zero] at hab; omega
    have hb2 : 2 ≤ b := (Nat.two_le_iff b).2 ⟨hb0, hb1⟩
    have ha2 : 2 ≤ p ^ k := by
      calc 2 ≤ p := hp.two_le
        _ = p ^ 1 := (pow_one p).symm
        _ ≤ p ^ k := Nat.pow_le_pow_right hp.one_le hk
    have hale : p ^ k ≤ n := by
      have h2 : p ^ k * 2 ≤ p ^ k * b := Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ hb2
      omega
    have hble : b ≤ n := by
      have h2 : 2 * b ≤ p ^ k * b := Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ ha2
      omega
    have hdvdN : (n + 1) ∣ LN n := by
      rw [← hab]
      exact hcop.mul_dvd_of_dvd_of_dvd (dvd_LN (by omega) hale) (dvd_LN (by omega) hble)
    rw [LN_succ, JN_of_not_isPrimePow hpp, one_mul]
    exact Nat.dvd_antisymm (Nat.lcm_dvd dvd_rfl hdvdN) (Nat.dvd_lcm_left _ _)

/-- **`JN_eq_div`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  `J_N` really is the quotient `L_N / L_{N-1}`. -/
theorem JN_eq_div (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) : JN (n + 1) = LN (n + 1) / LN n := by
  rw [LN_succ_eq n hn, Nat.mul_div_assoc _ dvd_rfl, Nat.div_self (LN_pos n), mul_one]

/-! ## D.15  Exact layer quotients and their fibrewise aggregation -/

/-- The exact layer carry `C_q = T_q / q`, meaningful exactly when `q ∣ T_q`. -/
def layerCarry (T q : ℤ) : ℤ := T / q

/-- **`layerCarry_exact`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  When `q ∣ T_q` the layer carry reproduces
`T_q` exactly. -/
theorem layerCarry_exact {T q : ℤ} (h : q ∣ T) : q * layerCarry T q = T := by
  rw [layerCarry, Int.mul_ediv_cancel' h]

/-- **`layerCarry_not_exact_without_dvd`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED` firewall.  Without the
divisibility hypothesis the layer quotient is *not* exact: `q = 2`, `T = 1`. -/
theorem layerCarry_not_exact_without_dvd : (2 : ℤ) * layerCarry 1 2 ≠ 1 := by decide

/-- The aggregated carry of the layer `⌊M/q⌋ = N`. -/
def aggregateCarry (M : ℕ) (Q : Finset ℕ) (Cq : ℕ → ℤ) (N : ℕ) : ℤ :=
  ∑ q ∈ Q.filter (fun q => M / q = N), Cq q

/-- **`carry_aggregate`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The exact aggregate identity: summing the layer
carries over the fibres `⌊M/q⌋ = N` recovers the total carry. -/
theorem carry_aggregate (M : ℕ) (Q : Finset ℕ) (Cq : ℕ → ℤ) (Ns : Finset ℕ)
    (hmaps : ∀ q ∈ Q, M / q ∈ Ns) :
    ∑ N ∈ Ns, aggregateCarry M Q Cq N = ∑ q ∈ Q, Cq q :=
  Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to hmaps Cq

/-! ## D.16  The descending exact recurrence -/

/-- **`descending_recurrence`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  If `z_N = J_N · z_{N-1} + C_N` with
`J_N ≠ 0`, then `J_N ∣ z_N − C_N` and `z_{N-1} = (z_N − C_N)/J_N`. -/
theorem descending_recurrence {z zprev C J : ℤ} (hJ : J ≠ 0) (h : z = J * zprev + C) :
    J ∣ (z - C) ∧ (z - C) / J = zprev := by
  have hz : z - C = J * zprev := by rw [h]; ring
  refine ⟨⟨zprev, hz⟩, ?_⟩
  rw [hz, Int.mul_ediv_cancel_left _ hJ]

/-- **`descending_step_iff`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The exact solvability criterion of one
descending step. -/
theorem descending_step_iff {z C J : ℤ} (hJ : J ≠ 0) :
    (∃ zprev : ℤ, z = J * zprev + C) ↔ J ∣ (z - C) := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨zprev, h⟩; exact (descending_recurrence hJ h).1
  · rintro ⟨t, ht⟩; exact ⟨t, by omega⟩

end Direct
end Erdos287

@@BEGIN_FILE bytes=9147 sha256=c69f7aef4da673f8dc1960b94b69b7da55cf542b1b1e3330d35e980bb02ed21c path=LEAN_PROJECT/RequestProject/Erdos287/Direct/LargePrimeCompletionFinite.lean@@
import RequestProject.Erdos287.Direct.PathPolynomial

/-!
# Route D — the finite all-target reciprocal lemma (finite Fourier adapter)

INTERNAL #287 RESEARCH PROGRAMME ONLY.  **Erdős #287 is `OPEN` here and is not claimed.**

This module proves, *in the kernel*, the finite Fourier adapter used by the simultaneous
prime-component completion step, and isolates the analytic input as an interface
proposition — never as an axiom.

* `subsetSumCount q C a t` counts the binary selections `S ⊆ C` with `∑_{n ∈ S} a n = t`
  in `ZMod q`.
* `char_sum_identity` is the exact finite Fourier identity
  `q · N(t) = ∑_ψ ψ(−t) ∏_{n ∈ C} (1 + ψ(a n))`, the sum running over all additive
  characters of `ZMod q`.
* `subsetSumCount_pos_of_bound` is the sufficient condition: if every nontrivial character
  product is `≤ B` in absolute value and `(q − 1)·B < 2^{|C|}`, then **every** target is
  attained.
* `ReciprocalExpSumInterface` is the (external, unformalised) exponential-sum input for the
  reciprocal system `a n = n⁻¹`; `allTargets_of_expSumInterface` is the deterministic
  consumer.  The interface is a hypothesis of the theorem, not an axiom of the file.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace Erdos287
namespace Direct

/-! ## D.22  Binary subset sums in `ZMod q` -/

variable {q : ℕ}

/-- The number of binary selections from `C` whose `a`-sum equals the target `t`. -/
def subsetSumCount (q : ℕ) (C : Finset ℕ) (a : ℕ → ZMod q) (t : ZMod q) : ℕ :=
  (C.powerset.filter (fun S => ∑ n ∈ S, a n = t)).card

/-- **`subsetSumCount_pos_iff`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Positivity of the count is exactly
attainability of the target. -/
theorem subsetSumCount_pos_iff (q : ℕ) (C : Finset ℕ) (a : ℕ → ZMod q) (t : ZMod q) :
    0 < subsetSumCount q C a t ↔ ∃ S ⊆ C, ∑ n ∈ S, a n = t := by
  rw [subsetSumCount, Finset.card_pos]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨S, hS⟩
    rw [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_powerset] at hS
    exact ⟨S, hS.1, hS.2⟩
  · rintro ⟨S, hSC, hS⟩
    exact ⟨S, Finset.mem_filter.2 ⟨Finset.mem_powerset.2 hSC, hS⟩⟩

theorem addChar_sum_eq_prod {A : Type*} [AddCommGroup A] (ψ : AddChar A ℂ) (s : Finset ℕ)
    (f : ℕ → A) : ψ (∑ i ∈ s, f i) = ∏ i ∈ s, ψ (f i) := by
  classical
  induction s using Finset.induction with
  | empty => simp
  | insert a s ha ih => rw [Finset.sum_insert ha, Finset.prod_insert ha, ψ.map_add_eq_mul, ih]

/-- **`prod_one_add_eq_sum_subsets`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Expansion of the character product
over binary selections. -/
theorem prod_one_add_eq_sum_subsets (C : Finset ℕ) (x : ℕ → ℂ) :
    ∏ n ∈ C, (1 + x n) = ∑ S ∈ C.powerset, ∏ n ∈ S, x n := by
  classical
  have := Finset.prod_add x (fun _ => (1 : ℂ)) C
  simp only [mul_one, Finset.prod_const_one] at this
  simpa [add_comm] using this

/-- **`char_sum_identity`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The exact finite Fourier identity for the
number of binary subset sums hitting a prescribed target of `ZMod q`. -/
theorem char_sum_identity [NeZero q] (C : Finset ℕ) (a : ℕ → ZMod q) (t : ZMod q) :
    (q : ℂ) * (subsetSumCount q C a t : ℂ) =
      ∑ ψ : AddChar (ZMod q) ℂ, ψ (-t) * ∏ n ∈ C, (1 + ψ (a n)) := by
  classical
  have hcard : (Fintype.card (ZMod q) : ℂ) = (q : ℂ) := by rw [ZMod.card q]
  calc (q : ℂ) * (subsetSumCount q C a t : ℂ)
      = ∑ S ∈ C.powerset, (if (∑ n ∈ S, a n) - t = 0 then (Fintype.card (ZMod q) : ℂ) else 0) := by
        rw [subsetSumCount, Finset.card_filter]
        push_cast
        rw [Finset.mul_sum]
        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun S _ => ?_
        by_cases h : (∑ n ∈ S, a n) = t
        · simp [h]
        · have h' : (∑ n ∈ S, a n) - t ≠ 0 := sub_ne_zero_of_ne h
          simp [h, h']
    _ = ∑ S ∈ C.powerset, ∑ ψ : AddChar (ZMod q) ℂ, ψ ((∑ n ∈ S, a n) - t) := by
        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun S _ => ?_
        rw [AddChar.sum_apply_eq_ite]
    _ = ∑ ψ : AddChar (ZMod q) ℂ, ∑ S ∈ C.powerset, ψ (-t) * ∏ n ∈ S, ψ (a n) := by
        rw [Finset.sum_comm]
        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun chi _ => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun S _ => ?_
        rw [show (∑ n ∈ S, a n) - t = (-t) + ∑ n ∈ S, a n by ring, chi.map_add_eq_mul,
          addChar_sum_eq_prod]
    _ = ∑ ψ : AddChar (ZMod q) ℂ, ψ (-t) * ∏ n ∈ C, (1 + ψ (a n)) := by
        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun ψ _ => ?_
        rw [← Finset.mul_sum, prod_one_add_eq_sum_subsets]

/-! ## D.23  The sufficient condition: every target is attained -/

/-- **`subsetSumCount_pos_of_bound`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  If every nontrivial character
product is bounded by `B` and `(q − 1)·B < 2^{|C|}`, then every target of `ZMod q` is a binary
subset sum of `a` over `C`. -/
theorem subsetSumCount_pos_of_bound [NeZero q] (C : Finset ℕ) (a : ℕ → ZMod q) (B : ℝ)
    (hB : ∀ ψ : AddChar (ZMod q) ℂ, ψ ≠ 0 → ‖∏ n ∈ C, (1 + ψ (a n))‖ ≤ B)
    (hlt : ((q : ℝ) - 1) * B < 2 ^ C.card) (t : ZMod q) :
    0 < subsetSumCount q C a t := by
  classical
  set F : AddChar (ZMod q) ℂ → ℂ := fun ψ => ψ (-t) * ∏ n ∈ C, (1 + ψ (a n)) with hF
  have hsplit : ∑ ψ : AddChar (ZMod q) ℂ, F ψ
      = F 0 + ∑ ψ ∈ (Finset.univ.erase (0 : AddChar (ZMod q) ℂ)), F ψ :=
    (Finset.add_sum_erase _ _ (Finset.mem_univ (0 : AddChar (ZMod q) ℂ))).symm
  have hF0 : F 0 = (2 : ℂ) ^ C.card := by
    simp [hF, AddChar.zero_apply]
    norm_num
  -- the nontrivial characters contribute at most `(q-1)·B`
  have hcardChar : (Finset.univ.erase (0 : AddChar (ZMod q) ℂ)).card = q - 1 := by
    rw [Finset.card_erase_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ _), Finset.card_univ, AddChar.card_eq,
      ZMod.card]
  have hbound : ‖∑ ψ ∈ (Finset.univ.erase (0 : AddChar (ZMod q) ℂ)), F ψ‖ ≤ ((q : ℝ) - 1) * B := by
    have hq1 : (1 : ℕ) ≤ q := Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.2 (NeZero.ne q)
    calc ‖∑ ψ ∈ (Finset.univ.erase (0 : AddChar (ZMod q) ℂ)), F ψ‖
        ≤ ∑ ψ ∈ (Finset.univ.erase (0 : AddChar (ZMod q) ℂ)), ‖F ψ‖ := norm_sum_le _ _
      _ ≤ ∑ _ψ ∈ (Finset.univ.erase (0 : AddChar (ZMod q) ℂ)), B := by
          refine Finset.sum_le_sum fun ψ hψ => ?_
          have hψ0 : ψ ≠ 0 := Finset.ne_of_mem_erase hψ
          rw [hF]
          simp only [norm_mul, AddChar.norm_apply, one_mul]
          exact hB ψ hψ0
      _ = ((q : ℕ) - 1 : ℕ) * B := by rw [Finset.sum_const, hcardChar, nsmul_eq_mul]
      _ = ((q : ℝ) - 1) * B := by
          congr 1
          have hcast : ((q - 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) = (q : ℝ) - 1 := by
            have := Nat.cast_sub (R := ℝ) hq1
            simpa using this
          rw [hcast]
  -- hence the total is positive
  have hid := char_sum_identity C a t
  rw [← hF] at hid
  rw [hsplit, hF0] at hid
  have hre : (2 : ℝ) ^ C.card - ((q : ℝ) - 1) * B ≤ ‖(q : ℂ) * (subsetSumCount q C a t : ℂ)‖ := by
    have h2 : ‖(2 : ℂ) ^ C.card‖ = (2 : ℝ) ^ C.card := by
      rw [norm_pow]; norm_num
    have h1 : ‖(2 : ℂ) ^ C.card‖ ≤ ‖(q : ℂ) * (subsetSumCount q C a t : ℂ)‖ +
        ‖∑ ψ ∈ (Finset.univ.erase (0 : AddChar (ZMod q) ℂ)), F ψ‖ := by
      have hsub : (2 : ℂ) ^ C.card
          = ((q : ℂ) * (subsetSumCount q C a t : ℂ))
            - ∑ ψ ∈ (Finset.univ.erase (0 : AddChar (ZMod q) ℂ)), F ψ := by
        rw [hid]; ring
      rw [hsub]
      exact norm_sub_le _ _
    rw [h2] at h1
    linarith [hbound]
  have hpos : (0 : ℝ) < ‖(q : ℂ) * (subsetSumCount q C a t : ℂ)‖ := by linarith
  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos (subsetSumCount q C a t) with h0 | h0
  · rw [h0] at hpos; simp at hpos
  · exact h0

/-! ## D.24  The analytic interface and its deterministic consumer -/

/-- **Interface (external, unformalised): reciprocal exponential-sum bound.**  The
Bourgain–Garaev-type input asserting that every nontrivial additive character product over the
reciprocal system `n ↦ n⁻¹ (mod q)` on the reservoir `C` is at most `B` in modulus.  This is an
*explicit hypothesis*: no axiom asserts it anywhere in this project. -/
def ReciprocalExpSumInterface (q : ℕ) (C : Finset ℕ) (B : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ ψ : AddChar (ZMod q) ℂ, ψ ≠ 0 → ‖∏ n ∈ C, (1 + ψ ((n : ZMod q)⁻¹))‖ ≤ B

/-- Every residue is an inverse binary subset sum of the reservoir `C`. -/
def AttainsAllTargets (q : ℕ) (C : Finset ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ t : ZMod q, ∃ S ⊆ C, ∑ n ∈ S, (n : ZMod q)⁻¹ = t

/-- **`allTargets_of_expSumInterface`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED` bridge, `CONDITIONAL` on the
exponential-sum interface: under the interface bound and the size condition
`(q − 1)·B < 2^{|C|}`, the reservoir attains every target. -/
theorem allTargets_of_expSumInterface [NeZero q] {C : Finset ℕ} {B : ℝ}
    (hBG : ReciprocalExpSumInterface q C B) (hlt : ((q : ℝ) - 1) * B < 2 ^ C.card) :
    AttainsAllTargets q C := by
  intro t
  have := subsetSumCount_pos_of_bound C (fun n => (n : ZMod q)⁻¹) B hBG hlt t
  exact (subsetSumCount_pos_iff q C (fun n => (n : ZMod q)⁻¹) t).1 this

end Direct
end Erdos287

@@END_FILE@@
@@BEGIN_FILE bytes=14714 sha256=e4365340d2223822a85ca63826dabb85c2daab29977c177db6598006f4369a29 path=LEAN_PROJECT/RequestProject/Erdos287/Direct/PathPolynomial.lean@@
import RequestProject.Erdos287.Direct.LCMCarry

/-!
# Route D — the physical path polynomial

INTERNAL #287 RESEARCH PROGRAMME ONLY.  **Erdős #287 is `OPEN` here and is not claimed.**

Given a set `V` of free positions and integral weights `w`, the *physical path polynomial* is

`P_V(X) = ∑_{J ⊆ V, J has no two consecutive positions} X^{∑_{n ∈ J} w n}`.

The exponents are integral by construction: the intended instantiation is `w n = ℓ / n` for a
common multiple `ℓ` of the positions, so `X^τ` tracks the exact cleared-denominator value of
the reciprocal sum.

Kernel-proved here:

* `pathPoly_coeff` — the `τ`-th coefficient counts the admissible independent sets of weight `τ`;
* `pathPoly_coeff_pos_iff` — positivity of the coefficient is exactly solvability;
* `exact_reciprocal_target` — **the exact target theorem**:
  `∑_{n ∈ P ∪ J} 1/n = 1 ↔ [X^τ] P_V(X)` counts `J`, i.e. the reciprocal equation for a pinned
  set `P` completed by a free independent set `J` is *equivalent* to positivity of the
  coefficient of `X^τ`, where `τ` is the exact residual `ℓ − ∑_{n ∈ P} ℓ/n`;
* `pathPoly_recurrence` — the path (transfer-matrix) recurrence `F_i = F_{i-1} + X^{w_i} F_{i-2}`;
* `pathPoly_mul_of_separated` — the product factorisation across physically separated
  components.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace Erdos287
namespace Direct

/-! ## D.17  Independent (no-two-consecutive) subsets -/

/-- The admissible ("physical") subsets of `V`: no two consecutive positions. -/
def indepSubsets (V : Finset ℕ) : Finset (Finset ℕ) :=
  V.powerset.filter (fun J => ∀ n ∈ J, n + 1 ∉ J)

@[simp] theorem mem_indepSubsets {V J : Finset ℕ} :
    J ∈ indepSubsets V ↔ J ⊆ V ∧ ∀ n ∈ J, n + 1 ∉ J := by
  simp [indepSubsets, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_powerset]

/-- The integral weight of an admissible subset. -/
def weightSum (w : ℕ → ℕ) (J : Finset ℕ) : ℕ := ∑ n ∈ J, w n

/-- The physical path polynomial of the free set `V`. -/
noncomputable def pathPoly (V : Finset ℕ) (w : ℕ → ℕ) : Polynomial ℤ :=
  ∑ J ∈ indepSubsets V, Polynomial.X ^ (weightSum w J)

/-! ## D.18  Coefficients -/

/-- **`pathPoly_coeff`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The `τ`-th coefficient of the path polynomial is
the number of admissible subsets of weight `τ`. -/
theorem pathPoly_coeff (V : Finset ℕ) (w : ℕ → ℕ) (τ : ℕ) :
    (pathPoly V w).coeff τ =
      (((indepSubsets V).filter (fun J => weightSum w J = τ)).card : ℤ) := by
  rw [pathPoly, Polynomial.finset_sum_coeff]
  simp only [Polynomial.coeff_X_pow]
  rw [Finset.sum_boole]
  congr 1
  refine congrArg Finset.card (Finset.filter_congr fun J _ => ?_)
  exact eq_comm

/-- **`pathPoly_coeff_pos_iff`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  A coefficient is positive exactly when
some admissible subset has that weight; coefficients are never negative. -/
theorem pathPoly_coeff_pos_iff (V : Finset ℕ) (w : ℕ → ℕ) (τ : ℕ) :
    0 < (pathPoly V w).coeff τ ↔ ∃ J ∈ indepSubsets V, weightSum w J = τ := by
  rw [pathPoly_coeff]
  constructor
  · intro h
    have hcard : 0 < ((indepSubsets V).filter (fun J => weightSum w J = τ)).card := by
      exact_mod_cast h
    obtain ⟨J, hJ⟩ := Finset.card_pos.1 hcard
    rw [Finset.mem_filter] at hJ
    exact ⟨J, hJ.1, hJ.2⟩
  · rintro ⟨J, hJ, hw⟩
    have hne : ((indepSubsets V).filter (fun J => weightSum w J = τ)).Nonempty :=
      ⟨J, Finset.mem_filter.2 ⟨hJ, hw⟩⟩
    exact_mod_cast Finset.card_pos.2 hne

/-! ## D.19  The exact reciprocal target -/

/-- **`recipSum_union_eq_one_iff`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  With a common multiple `ℓ` of all
positions, the reciprocal equation for `P ∪ J` is the exact integral weight equation for `J`. -/
theorem recipSum_union_eq_one_iff {P J : Finset ℕ} {ell τ : ℕ} (hell : ell ≠ 0)
    (hdisj : Disjoint P J)
    (hP : ∀ n ∈ P, n ≠ 0 ∧ n ∣ ell) (hJ : ∀ n ∈ J, n ≠ 0 ∧ n ∣ ell)
    (hτ : (∑ n ∈ P, ell / n) + τ = ell) :
    recipSum (P ∪ J) = 1 ↔ weightSum (fun n => ell / n) J = τ := by
  have hmem : ∀ n ∈ P ∪ J, n ≠ 0 ∧ n ∣ ell := by
    intro n hn
    rcases Finset.mem_union.1 hn with h | h
    · exact hP n h
    · exact hJ n h
  have hclear := clearing_identity (A := P ∪ J) (D := ell)
    (fun n hn => (hmem n hn).2) (fun n hn => (hmem n hn).1)
  have hsplit : (∑ n ∈ P ∪ J, ell / n) = (∑ n ∈ P, ell / n) + ∑ n ∈ J, ell / n :=
    Finset.sum_union hdisj
  have hellQ : (ell : ℚ) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.2 hell
  constructor
  · intro h
    rw [h, mul_one] at hclear
    have : (∑ n ∈ P ∪ J, ell / n) = ell := by exact_mod_cast hclear
    rw [hsplit] at this
    show (∑ n ∈ J, ell / n) = τ
    omega
  · intro h
    have h' : (∑ n ∈ J, ell / n) = τ := h
    have hnat : (∑ n ∈ P ∪ J, ell / n) = ell := by rw [hsplit, h']; omega
    rw [hnat] at hclear
    have : (ell : ℚ) = ell * recipSum (P ∪ J) := by exact_mod_cast hclear
    field_simp at this
    exact this.symm

/-- **`exact_reciprocal_target`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  *The* exact target theorem of Route D:
completing the pinned set `P` by a physical (no-two-consecutive) subset of the free set `V` to
reciprocal sum `1` is **equivalent** to positivity of the coefficient of `X^τ` in the path
polynomial, `τ` being the exact residual `ℓ − ∑_{n∈P} ℓ/n`. -/
theorem exact_reciprocal_target {P V : Finset ℕ} {ell τ : ℕ} (hell : ell ≠ 0)
    (hdisj : Disjoint P V)
    (hP : ∀ n ∈ P, n ≠ 0 ∧ n ∣ ell) (hV : ∀ n ∈ V, n ≠ 0 ∧ n ∣ ell)
    (hτ : (∑ n ∈ P, ell / n) + τ = ell) :
    (∃ J ∈ indepSubsets V, recipSum (P ∪ J) = 1) ↔
      0 < (pathPoly V (fun n => ell / n)).coeff τ := by
  rw [pathPoly_coeff_pos_iff]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨J, hJ, hsum⟩
    have hJV : J ⊆ V := (mem_indepSubsets.1 hJ).1
    refine ⟨J, hJ, ?_⟩
    exact (recipSum_union_eq_one_iff hell (Finset.disjoint_of_subset_right hJV hdisj) hP
      (fun n hn => hV n (hJV hn)) hτ).1 hsum
  · rintro ⟨J, hJ, hw⟩
    have hJV : J ⊆ V := (mem_indepSubsets.1 hJ).1
    refine ⟨J, hJ, ?_⟩
    exact (recipSum_union_eq_one_iff hell (Finset.disjoint_of_subset_right hJV hdisj) hP
      (fun n hn => hV n (hJV hn)) hτ).2 hw

/-! ## D.20  The path recurrence -/

theorem indepSubsets_filter_notMem (a j : ℕ) :
    (indepSubsets (Finset.Icc a (j + 1))).filter (fun J => (j + 1) ∉ J) =
      indepSubsets (Finset.Icc a j) := by
  ext J
  simp only [Finset.mem_filter, mem_indepSubsets]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨⟨hsub, hind⟩, hnot⟩
    refine ⟨fun n hn => ?_, hind⟩
    have := hsub hn
    rw [Finset.mem_Icc] at this ⊢
    refine ⟨this.1, ?_⟩
    rcases Nat.lt_or_ge n (j + 1) with h | h
    · omega
    · exact absurd (by omega : n = j + 1) (fun hEq => hnot (hEq ▸ hn))
  · rintro ⟨hsub, hind⟩
    refine ⟨⟨fun n hn => ?_, hind⟩, fun hmem => ?_⟩
    · have := hsub hn
      rw [Finset.mem_Icc] at this ⊢
      omega
    · have := hsub hmem
      rw [Finset.mem_Icc] at this
      omega

/-- **`pathPoly_recurrence`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The transfer-matrix recurrence along a
physical path: `F_{i} = F_{i-1} + X^{w_i} · F_{i-2}`. -/
theorem pathPoly_recurrence {a j : ℕ} (ha : 1 ≤ a) (haj : a ≤ j) (w : ℕ → ℕ) :
    pathPoly (Finset.Icc a (j + 1)) w =
      pathPoly (Finset.Icc a j) w + Polynomial.X ^ (w (j + 1)) * pathPoly (Finset.Icc a (j - 1)) w := by
  classical
  have hsplit :
      pathPoly (Finset.Icc a (j + 1)) w =
        (∑ J ∈ (indepSubsets (Finset.Icc a (j + 1))).filter (fun J => (j + 1) ∉ J),
          Polynomial.X ^ (weightSum w J)) +
        (∑ J ∈ (indepSubsets (Finset.Icc a (j + 1))).filter (fun J => (j + 1) ∈ J),
          Polynomial.X ^ (weightSum w J)) := by
    rw [pathPoly, ← Finset.sum_filter_add_sum_filter_not _ (fun J => (j + 1) ∉ J)]
    simp
  rw [hsplit, indepSubsets_filter_notMem a j]
  congr 1
  -- the sets containing `j+1` biject with the admissible subsets of `[a, j-1]`
  · rw [pathPoly, Finset.mul_sum]
    refine (Finset.sum_nbij' (fun K => insert (j + 1) K) (fun J => J.erase (j + 1))
      ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_).symm
    · intro K hK
      show insert (j + 1) K ∈ _
      rw [Finset.mem_filter, mem_indepSubsets]
      simp only [mem_indepSubsets] at hK
      obtain ⟨hsub, hind⟩ := hK
      have hKb : ∀ n ∈ K, a ≤ n ∧ n ≤ j - 1 := by
        intro n hn; have := hsub hn; rw [Finset.mem_Icc] at this; exact this
      refine ⟨⟨fun n hn => ?_, fun n hn => ?_⟩, Finset.mem_insert_self _ _⟩
      · rcases Finset.mem_insert.1 hn with rfl | hn
        · rw [Finset.mem_Icc]; omega
        · have := hKb n hn; rw [Finset.mem_Icc]; omega
      · rcases Finset.mem_insert.1 hn with rfl | hn'
        · intro hmem
          rcases Finset.mem_insert.1 hmem with h | h
          · omega
          · have := hKb _ h; omega
        · have hnb := hKb n hn'
          intro hmem
          rcases Finset.mem_insert.1 hmem with h | h
          · omega
          · exact hind n hn' h
    · intro J hJ
      rw [Finset.mem_filter, mem_indepSubsets] at hJ
      obtain ⟨⟨hsub, hind⟩, hmem⟩ := hJ
      show J.erase (j + 1) ∈ _
      rw [mem_indepSubsets]
      refine ⟨fun n hn => ?_, fun n hn => ?_⟩
      · have hn' : n ∈ J := Finset.mem_of_mem_erase hn
        have hne : n ≠ j + 1 := Finset.ne_of_mem_erase hn
        have hb := hsub hn'
        rw [Finset.mem_Icc] at hb ⊢
        refine ⟨hb.1, ?_⟩
        rcases Nat.lt_or_ge n j with h | h
        · omega
        · exfalso
          have : n = j := by omega
          subst this
          exact hind n hn' (by simpa using hmem)
      · intro hcon
        exact hind n (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase hn) (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase hcon)
    · intro K hK
      simp only [mem_indepSubsets] at hK
      have hKb : ∀ n ∈ K, a ≤ n ∧ n ≤ j - 1 := by
        intro n hn; have := hK.1 hn; rw [Finset.mem_Icc] at this; exact this
      have hnotK : (j + 1) ∉ K := by
        intro hmem; have := hKb _ hmem; omega
      show (insert (j + 1) K).erase (j + 1) = K
      rw [Finset.erase_insert hnotK]
    · intro J hJ
      rw [Finset.mem_filter] at hJ
      show insert (j + 1) (J.erase (j + 1)) = J
      exact Finset.insert_erase hJ.2
    · intro K hK
      simp only [mem_indepSubsets] at hK
      have hKb : ∀ n ∈ K, a ≤ n ∧ n ≤ j - 1 := by
        intro n hn; have := hK.1 hn; rw [Finset.mem_Icc] at this; exact this
      have hnot : (j + 1) ∉ K := by
        intro hmem; have := hKb _ hmem; omega
      show Polynomial.X ^ (w (j + 1)) * Polynomial.X ^ (weightSum w K)
        = Polynomial.X ^ (weightSum w (insert (j + 1) K))
      have hws : weightSum w (insert (j + 1) K) = w (j + 1) + weightSum w K := by
        simp [weightSum, Finset.sum_insert hnot]
      rw [hws, pow_add]

/-! ## D.21  Factorisation across physically separated components -/

/-- Two position sets are *physically separated* when they are disjoint and no position of one
is adjacent to a position of the other. -/
def Separated (V₁ V₂ : Finset ℕ) : Prop :=
  Disjoint V₁ V₂ ∧ ∀ n ∈ V₁, ∀ m ∈ V₂, n + 1 ≠ m ∧ m + 1 ≠ n

/-- **`pathPoly_mul_of_separated`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The path polynomial factorises across
physically separated components. -/
theorem pathPoly_mul_of_separated {V₁ V₂ : Finset ℕ} (h : Separated V₁ V₂) (w : ℕ → ℕ) :
    pathPoly (V₁ ∪ V₂) w = pathPoly V₁ w * pathPoly V₂ w := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨hdisj, hadj⟩ := h
  rw [pathPoly, pathPoly, pathPoly, Finset.sum_mul_sum, ← Finset.sum_product']
  refine (Finset.sum_nbij' (fun p : Finset ℕ × Finset ℕ => p.1 ∪ p.2)
    (fun J => (J ∩ V₁, J ∩ V₂)) ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_).symm
  · rintro ⟨J₁, J₂⟩ hp
    rw [Finset.mem_product] at hp
    obtain ⟨hs₁, hi₁⟩ := mem_indepSubsets.1 hp.1
    obtain ⟨hs₂, hi₂⟩ := mem_indepSubsets.1 hp.2
    show J₁ ∪ J₂ ∈ indepSubsets (V₁ ∪ V₂)
    rw [mem_indepSubsets]
    refine ⟨Finset.union_subset (hs₁.trans Finset.subset_union_left)
      (hs₂.trans Finset.subset_union_right), ?_⟩
    intro n hn hcon
    rcases Finset.mem_union.1 hn with hn₁ | hn₂
    · rcases Finset.mem_union.1 hcon with hc₁ | hc₂
      · exact hi₁ n hn₁ hc₁
      · exact (hadj n (hs₁ hn₁) (n + 1) (hs₂ hc₂)).1 rfl
    · rcases Finset.mem_union.1 hcon with hc₁ | hc₂
      · exact (hadj (n + 1) (hs₁ hc₁) n (hs₂ hn₂)).2 rfl
      · exact hi₂ n hn₂ hc₂
  · intro J hJ
    obtain ⟨hsub, hind⟩ := mem_indepSubsets.1 hJ
    show ((J ∩ V₁, J ∩ V₂) : Finset ℕ × Finset ℕ) ∈ indepSubsets V₁ ×ˢ indepSubsets V₂
    rw [Finset.mem_product]
    constructor <;>
      · rw [mem_indepSubsets]
        refine ⟨Finset.inter_subset_right, fun n hn hcon => ?_⟩
        exact hind n (Finset.mem_of_mem_inter_left hn) (Finset.mem_of_mem_inter_left hcon)
  · rintro ⟨J₁, J₂⟩ hp
    rw [Finset.mem_product] at hp
    have hs₁ : J₁ ⊆ V₁ := (mem_indepSubsets.1 hp.1).1
    have hs₂ : J₂ ⊆ V₂ := (mem_indepSubsets.1 hp.2).1
    show ((J₁ ∪ J₂) ∩ V₁, (J₁ ∪ J₂) ∩ V₂) = (J₁, J₂)
    have h1 : (J₁ ∪ J₂) ∩ V₁ = J₁ := by
      ext x
      simp only [Finset.mem_inter, Finset.mem_union]
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨hx | hx, hxV⟩
        · exact hx
        · exact absurd hxV (Finset.disjoint_right.1 hdisj (hs₂ hx))
      · intro hx; exact ⟨Or.inl hx, hs₁ hx⟩
    have h2 : (J₁ ∪ J₂) ∩ V₂ = J₂ := by
      ext x
      simp only [Finset.mem_inter, Finset.mem_union]
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨hx | hx, hxV⟩
        · exact absurd hxV (Finset.disjoint_left.1 hdisj (hs₁ hx))
        · exact hx
      · intro hx; exact ⟨Or.inr hx, hs₂ hx⟩
    rw [h1, h2]
  · intro J hJ
    obtain ⟨hsub, -⟩ := mem_indepSubsets.1 hJ
    show J ∩ V₁ ∪ J ∩ V₂ = J
    rw [← Finset.inter_union_distrib_left]
    exact Finset.inter_eq_left.2 hsub
  · rintro ⟨J₁, J₂⟩ hp
    rw [Finset.mem_product] at hp
    have hs₁ : J₁ ⊆ V₁ := (mem_indepSubsets.1 hp.1).1
    have hs₂ : J₂ ⊆ V₂ := (mem_indepSubsets.1 hp.2).1
    have hdJ : Disjoint J₁ J₂ :=
      Finset.disjoint_of_subset_left hs₁ (Finset.disjoint_of_subset_right hs₂ hdisj)
    show Polynomial.X ^ (weightSum w J₁) * Polynomial.X ^ (weightSum w J₂)
      = Polynomial.X ^ (weightSum w (J₁ ∪ J₂))
    have hws : weightSum w (J₁ ∪ J₂) = weightSum w J₁ + weightSum w J₂ := by
      simp [weightSum, Finset.sum_union hdJ]
    rw [hws, pow_add]

end Direct
end Erdos287

@@END_FILE@@
@@BEGIN_FILE bytes=10843 sha256=c960cfdf0a4bee00979ee4028d61e9dc7b120c8298563ff857f7cdf68d1c3d88 path=LEAN_PROJECT/RequestProject/Erdos287/Direct/ProtectedSwitches.lean@@
import RequestProject.Erdos287.Direct.ReciprocalCompiler

/-!
# Route D — protected switches (value-preserving and value-moving)

INTERNAL #287 RESEARCH PROGRAMME ONLY.  **Erdős #287 is `OPEN` here and is not claimed.**

Two kinds of local moves are formalised exactly.

**Value-preserving.**  The identity `1/(6k) = 1/(10k) + 1/(15k)` and precisely what it
preserves: the rational value always; the *cleared-denominator carry coordinates* only under
the explicit divisibility hypothesis `30k ∣ D` (`carry_neutral_of_dvd`), and
`carry_not_neutral_without_dvd` shows that hypothesis cannot be dropped.  Cardinality is *not*
preserved (`switch_changes_card`).

**Value-moving.**  The exact signed increment `1/(ck) − 1/(dk) = (d−c)/(cdk)`, and an abstract
`ProtectedSwitch` predicate collecting all the local conditions (support inside the interval,
no adjacency conflict, neighbour protection, non-collision with the swapped-in site).  From the
predicate we prove: the toggle preserves the endpoint pins and the no-two-consecutive-omissions
rule, preserves every additive tracked statistic that agrees on the two sites, and changes the
reciprocal value by exactly the stated increment.

Supply/abundance of switches is deliberately **not** part of these theorems: it is an analytic
input, kept as an interface in `Direct/TargetTuningFinite.lean`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace Erdos287
namespace Direct

/-! ## D.30  The value-preserving switch -/

/-- **`sixSwitch_identity`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  `1/(6k) = 1/(10k) + 1/(15k)`. -/
theorem sixSwitch_identity (k : ℚ) (hk : k ≠ 0) :
    1 / (6 * k) = 1 / (10 * k) + 1 / (15 * k) := by
  field_simp
  ring

/-- **`recipSum_sixSwitch`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Performing the switch inside a selection
preserves the reciprocal sum exactly. -/
theorem recipSum_sixSwitch {A : Finset ℕ} {k : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k) (h6 : 6 * k ∈ A)
    (h10 : 10 * k ∉ A) (h15 : 15 * k ∉ A) :
    recipSum (insert (10 * k) (insert (15 * k) (A.erase (6 * k)))) = recipSum A := by
  have hk' : (k : ℚ) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.2 (by omega)
  have h15' : 15 * k ∉ A.erase (6 * k) := fun h => h15 (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase h)
  have h10' : 10 * k ∉ insert (15 * k) (A.erase (6 * k)) := by
    intro h
    rcases Finset.mem_insert.1 h with h' | h'
    · omega
    · exact h10 (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase h')
  rw [recipSum_insert h10', recipSum_insert h15']
  have herase : recipSum A = 1 / ((6 * k : ℕ) : ℚ) + recipSum (A.erase (6 * k)) := by
    rw [← recipSum_insert (Finset.notMem_erase _ _), Finset.insert_erase h6]
  rw [herase]
  push_cast
  rw [sixSwitch_identity (k : ℚ) hk']
  ring

/-- **`carry_neutral_of_dvd`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Under the explicit divisibility hypothesis
`30k ∣ D`, the switch is neutral on the cleared-denominator (carry) coordinates. -/
theorem carry_neutral_of_dvd {D k : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k) (h : 30 * k ∣ D) :
    D / (6 * k) = D / (10 * k) + D / (15 * k) := by
  obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := h
  have h1 : 30 * k * c / (6 * k) = 5 * c := by
    rw [show 30 * k * c = (6 * k) * (5 * c) by ring, Nat.mul_div_cancel_left _ (by omega)]
  have h2 : 30 * k * c / (10 * k) = 3 * c := by
    rw [show 30 * k * c = (10 * k) * (3 * c) by ring, Nat.mul_div_cancel_left _ (by omega)]
  have h3 : 30 * k * c / (15 * k) = 2 * c := by
    rw [show 30 * k * c = (15 * k) * (2 * c) by ring, Nat.mul_div_cancel_left _ (by omega)]
  rw [h1, h2, h3]
  ring

/-- **`carry_not_neutral_without_dvd`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED` firewall.  Without `30k ∣ D` carry
neutrality genuinely fails: `D = 6`, `k = 1` gives `1 ≠ 0`. -/
theorem carry_not_neutral_without_dvd :
    (6 : ℕ) / (6 * 1) ≠ 6 / (10 * 1) + 6 / (15 * 1) := by decide

/-- **`switch_changes_card`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED` firewall.  The switch is *not* neutral on the
cardinality of the selection: it increases it by one. -/
theorem switch_changes_card {A : Finset ℕ} {k : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k) (h6 : 6 * k ∈ A)
    (h10 : 10 * k ∉ A) (h15 : 15 * k ∉ A) :
    (insert (10 * k) (insert (15 * k) (A.erase (6 * k)))).card = A.card + 1 := by
  have h15' : 15 * k ∉ A.erase (6 * k) := fun h => h15 (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase h)
  have h10' : 10 * k ∉ insert (15 * k) (A.erase (6 * k)) := by
    intro h
    rcases Finset.mem_insert.1 h with h' | h'
    · omega
    · exact h10 (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase h')
  rw [Finset.card_insert_of_notMem h10', Finset.card_insert_of_notMem h15',
    Finset.card_erase_of_mem h6]
  have : 1 ≤ A.card := Finset.card_pos.2 ⟨_, h6⟩
  omega

/-! ## D.31  The value-moving switch -/

/-- **`movingSwitch_increment`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The exact signed increment. -/
theorem movingSwitch_increment (c d k : ℚ) (hc : c ≠ 0) (hd : d ≠ 0) (hk : k ≠ 0) :
    1 / (c * k) - 1 / (d * k) = (d - c) / (c * d * k) := by
  field_simp

/-- The toggle that removes the position `out` from the selection and adds the position `inn`. -/
def toggle (eps : ℕ → Bool) (out inn : ℕ) : ℕ → Bool :=
  fun n => if n = out then false else if n = inn then true else eps n

/-- **The local conditions of a protected switch.**  Support inside the interval, the removed
site strictly interior (so the endpoint pins survive), no adjacency conflict (both neighbours of
the removed site are selected), and non-collision of the two sites. -/
structure ProtectedSwitch (a M : ℕ) (eps : ℕ → Bool) (out inn : ℕ) : Prop where
  /-- the removed site is currently selected -/
  out_sel : eps out = true
  /-- the added site is currently free -/
  inn_free : eps inn = false
  /-- the removed site is strictly interior -/
  out_interior : a < out ∧ out < M
  /-- the added site lies in the interval -/
  inn_range : a ≤ inn ∧ inn ≤ M
  /-- the two sites are distinct -/
  sites_ne : out ≠ inn
  /-- left neighbour protection -/
  left_guard : eps (out - 1) = true
  /-- right neighbour protection -/
  right_guard : eps (out + 1) = true

variable {a M : ℕ} {eps : ℕ → Bool} {out inn : ℕ}

/-- **`toggle_preserves_endpoints`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`. -/
theorem toggle_preserves_endpoints (hs : ProtectedSwitch a M eps out inn)
    (hend : EndpointSelected a M eps) : EndpointSelected a M (toggle eps out inn) := by
  obtain ⟨hlo, hhi⟩ := hs.out_interior
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · simp only [toggle]
    rw [if_neg (by omega)]
    by_cases h : a = inn
    · rw [if_pos h]
    · rw [if_neg h]; exact hend.1
  · simp only [toggle]
    rw [if_neg (by omega)]
    by_cases h : M = inn
    · rw [if_pos h]
    · rw [if_neg h]; exact hend.2

/-- **`toggle_preserves_isolation`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  A protected switch never creates two
consecutive omissions. -/
theorem toggle_preserves_isolation (hs : ProtectedSwitch a M eps out inn)
    (hiso : NoTwoConsecutiveOmissions a M eps) :
    NoTwoConsecutiveOmissions a M (toggle eps out inn) := by
  obtain ⟨hlo, hhi⟩ := hs.out_interior
  intro n hn hn'
  by_cases hout : n = out
  · right
    subst hout
    simp only [toggle]
    rw [if_neg (by omega)]
    by_cases h : n + 1 = inn
    · rw [if_pos h]
    · rw [if_neg h]; exact hs.right_guard
  · by_cases hout' : n + 1 = out
    · left
      simp only [toggle]
      rw [if_neg hout]
      by_cases h : n = inn
      · rw [if_pos h]
      · rw [if_neg h]
        have : n = out - 1 := by omega
        rw [this]; exact hs.left_guard
    · rcases hiso n hn hn' with h | h
      · left
        simp only [toggle]
        rw [if_neg hout]
        by_cases h' : n = inn
        · rw [if_pos h']
        · rw [if_neg h']; exact h
      · right
        simp only [toggle]
        rw [if_neg hout']
        by_cases h' : n + 1 = inn
        · rw [if_pos h']
        · rw [if_neg h']; exact h

/-- **`selected_toggle`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  The selected set after a protected switch. -/
theorem selected_toggle (hs : ProtectedSwitch a M eps out inn) :
    selected a M (toggle eps out inn) = insert inn ((selected a M eps).erase out) := by
  obtain ⟨hlo, hhi⟩ := hs.out_interior
  obtain ⟨hinnlo, hinnhi⟩ := hs.inn_range
  ext x
  simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_erase, mem_selected, toggle]
  constructor
  · intro hx
    obtain ⟨⟨hx1, hx2⟩, hx3⟩ := hx
    by_cases hxo : x = out
    · rw [if_pos hxo] at hx3; exact absurd hx3 (by simp)
    · rw [if_neg hxo] at hx3
      by_cases hxi : x = inn
      · exact Or.inl hxi
      · rw [if_neg hxi] at hx3
        exact Or.inr ⟨hxo, ⟨hx1, hx2⟩, hx3⟩
  · intro hx
    rcases hx with rfl | ⟨hxo, ⟨hx1, hx2⟩, hx3⟩
    · refine ⟨⟨hinnlo, hinnhi⟩, ?_⟩
      rw [if_neg (Ne.symm hs.sites_ne), if_pos rfl]
    · refine ⟨⟨hx1, hx2⟩, ?_⟩
      rw [if_neg hxo]
      by_cases hxi : x = inn
      · rw [if_pos hxi]
      · rw [if_neg hxi]; exact hx3

/-- **`recipSum_toggle`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  A protected switch moves the reciprocal value by
exactly `1/inn − 1/out`. -/
theorem recipSum_toggle (hs : ProtectedSwitch a M eps out inn) :
    recipSum (selected a M (toggle eps out inn)) =
      recipSum (selected a M eps) + 1 / (inn : ℚ) - 1 / (out : ℚ) := by
  obtain ⟨hlo, hhi⟩ := hs.out_interior
  obtain ⟨hinnlo, hinnhi⟩ := hs.inn_range
  have hout_mem : out ∈ selected a M eps :=
    mem_selected.2 ⟨⟨by omega, by omega⟩, hs.out_sel⟩
  have hinn_not : inn ∉ selected a M eps := by
    intro h
    have := (mem_selected.1 h).2
    rw [hs.inn_free] at this
    exact absurd this (by simp)
  have hinn_not' : inn ∉ (selected a M eps).erase out :=
    fun h => hinn_not (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase h)
  rw [selected_toggle hs, recipSum_insert hinn_not']
  have hsplit : recipSum (selected a M eps)
      = 1 / (out : ℚ) + recipSum ((selected a M eps).erase out) := by
    rw [← recipSum_insert (Finset.notMem_erase _ _), Finset.insert_erase hout_mem]
  rw [hsplit]
  ring

/-- **`tracked_sum_invariant`.**  `KERNEL-PROVED`.  Every additive tracked statistic that takes
the same value on the two sites is preserved by a protected switch. -/
theorem tracked_sum_invariant (hs : ProtectedSwitch a M eps out inn) (track : ℕ → ℤ)
    (hagree : track out = track inn) :
    ∑ n ∈ selected a M (toggle eps out inn), track n = ∑ n ∈ selected a M eps, track n := by
  obtain ⟨hlo, hhi⟩ := hs.out_interior
  obtain ⟨hinnlo, hinnhi⟩ := hs.inn_range
  have hout_mem : out ∈ selected a M eps :=
    mem_selected.2 ⟨⟨by omega, by omega⟩, hs.out_sel⟩
  have hinn_not : inn ∉ selected a M eps := by
    intro h
    have := (mem_selected.1 h).2
    rw [hs.inn_free] at this
    exact absurd this (by simp)
  have hinn_not' : inn ∉ (selected a M eps).erase out :=
    fun h => hinn_not (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase h)
  rw [selected_toggle hs, Finset.sum_insert hinn_not', ← hagree,
    ← Finset.sum_insert (Finset.notMem_erase out (selected a M eps)),
    Finset.insert_erase hout_mem]

end Direct
end Erdos287
