/-!
# Erdős #287 — Research Bank V29 §7.4: two-large branch composition

INTERNAL #287 RESEARCH PROGRAMME ONLY.  **Erdős #287 is `OPEN` here and is not claimed.**

## Audit finding

Identical to the one-large branch: `twoLarge : BranchClassBound Us Ur D2` with `D2`
UNINTERPRETED; no two-large coefficient sequence / modulus is built from the physical source in
V2–V28.  The field is kept as the external-shape `TwoLargeAnalyticProvider`; the identification
`D2 = physical two-large functional` is recorded as missing.

## Proved here (LEAN BANK)

* `twoLarge_sum_split` — box-wise composition (same argument as `oneLarge_sum_split`);
* `four_branch_sum_small` — the four branch class bounds (zero / one-large / two-large /
  boundary) give eventual smallness of the summed functional on every source decomposition with a
  fixed coefficient mass (reuse of the V28 `derived_source_class_provider` and V24
  `distribution_error_small`).
-/

namespace Erdos287
namespace ResearchBankV29
namespace TwoLargeComposition

open ResearchBankV22.IndependentFactorization ResearchBankV28.RepairedAnalyticBundle
open ResearchBankV24.RepairedProvider

/-- **Box-wise composition for the two-large branch** (LEAN BANK). -/
theorem twoLarge_sum_split {Us Ur : ℕ → ℕ → Finset ℕ} {D2 : ℕ → (Finset ℕ → ℝ) → ℝ}
    (P : BranchClassBound Us Ur D2) {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] (c : ι → ℝ) (S : ℕ) :
    ∀ ε > 0, ∃ M₀ : ℕ, ∀ M ≥ M₀, ∀ g : ι → Finset ℕ → ℝ,
      (∀ i, SourceFactorization (g i) (Us S M) (Ur S M)) →
      |D2 M (fun A => ∑ i, c i * g i A)| ≤ (∑ i, |c i|) * ε :=
  OneLargeComposition.oneLarge_sum_split P c S

/-- **Four-branch smallness** (LEAN CONDITIONAL on the four branch class bounds). -/
theorem four_branch_sum_small {Us Ur : ℕ → ℕ → Finset ℕ} {D0 D1 D2 Db : ℕ → (Finset ℕ → ℝ) → ℝ}
    (h0 : BranchClassBound Us Ur D0) (h1 : BranchClassBound Us Ur D1)
    (h2 : BranchClassBound Us Ur D2) (hb : BranchClassBound Us Ur Db) (S : ℕ)
    (lam : ℕ → Finset ℕ → ℝ) {Cm : ℝ} (hCm : 0 ≤ Cm)
    (hdec : ∀ M, SourceDecomposition (lam M) (Us S M) (Ur S M) Cm) :
    ∀ ε > 0, ∃ M₀ : ℕ, ∀ M ≥ M₀, |sumDE D0 D1 D2 Db M (lam M)| ≤ ε :=
  distribution_error_small (derived_source_class_provider h0 h1 h2 hb) S lam hCm hdec

end TwoLargeComposition
end ResearchBankV29
end Erdos287

/-!
# Erdős #287 — Research Bank V29 §7.2: Type-II branch composition

INTERNAL #287 RESEARCH PROGRAMME ONLY.  **Erdős #287 is `OPEN` here and is not claimed.**

## Audit finding

The V28 bundle has NO separate Type-II field: the Type-II (bilinear, DI) contribution is the
nonzero-frequency functional `DEnz`, which enters through
`nonzero : ∀ S τ M, NonzeroCleanRealization DIClass M (DEnz M (LamFam … S τ M)) Cnz`.
The V26 identities (Heath-Brown, rough convolution, product boxes, singleton bins, dyadic map,
trichotomy) are proved for explicit finite sums, but no declaration maps the physical pair source
through them to `DEnz`, and no clean state is generated (see `PhysicalCleanState`).  Therefore
the "branch already satisfies source contract" content is NOT eliminated; it is exactly the
`nonzero` field, kept inside the internal glue owner (`ProviderElimination`).

## Proved here (LEAN BANK / LEAN CONDITIONAL)

* `typeII_coverage` — the V26 structural trichotomy restated: every normalized HB exponent vector
  with `0 < α ≤ 2/5` is Type-II, one-large or two-large (so the three branch fields of V28 cover
  every source box once a source map exists);
* `typeII_branch_small_of_realization` — the V28 derived nonzero theorem, restated as the Type-II
  branch bound: DI provider + clean realizations ⟹ eventually `[DEnz]_+ ≤ ε`.
-/

namespace Erdos287
namespace ResearchBankV29
namespace TypeIIBranchComposition

open ResearchBankV26.HBBranchCoverage ResearchBankV27.DISpectral
  ResearchBankV28.RepairedAnalyticBundle

/-- **HB branch coverage** (LEAN BANK, V26 reuse). -/
theorem typeII_coverage {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] (s : Finset ι) (e : ι → ℝ)
    (he : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 ≤ e i) (hsum : ∑ i ∈ s, e i = 1) {α : ℝ} (hα : 0 < α) (hα' : α ≤ 2 / 5) :
    TypeII s e α ∨ OneLarge s e α ∨ TwoLarge s e α :=
  branch_trichotomy s e he hsum hα hα'

/-- **Type-II branch bound from clean realizations** (LEAN CONDITIONAL; V28 reuse). -/
theorem typeII_branch_small_of_realization {DIClass : KloostermanData → Prop} {Cnz : ℝ}
    (hDI : DISpectralProvider (1 / 1100) DIClass) (val : ℕ → ℝ)
    (hreal : ∀ M : ℕ, NonzeroCleanRealization DIClass M (val M) Cnz) :
    ∀ ε > 0, ∃ M₀ : ℕ, ∀ M ≥ M₀, max (val M) 0 ≤ ε :=
  nonzero_branch_small hDI val hreal

end TypeIIBranchComposition
end ResearchBankV29
end Erdos287

import RequestProject.Erdos287.ResearchBankV29.NonzeroPruning
import RequestProject.Erdos287.ResearchBankV25.LocalizationContract

/-!
# Erdős #287 — Research Bank V29 §7.1: zero-frequency / BDH branch composition

INTERNAL #287 RESEARCH PROGRAMME ONLY.  **Erdős #287 is `OPEN` here and is not claimed.**

## Audit finding

In V28 the zero-frequency branch enters ONLY as the field
`zeroFreq : BranchClassBound Us Ur D0` of `FinalAnalyticProviders`, for an UNINTERPRETED functional
`D0 : ℕ → (Finset ℕ → ℝ) → ℝ`.  The V25 chain (fixed-modulus centering, correction aggregation,
conditioned-energy projection, `zero_frequency_localized_bound`) bounds the explicit sum
`FullSum f Qs κ rq Ns γ` of a `ZeroFreqData`, but no declaration of V2–V28 defines `D0` in terms of
a `ZeroFreqData` built from the physical pair source.  Hence the zero branch bound cannot be
*derived* for `D0`: the `zeroFreq` field is kept, classified EXTERNAL-SHAPE (a masked SW/BDH class
bound) with the INTERNAL identification `D0 = physical zero-frequency functional` missing.

## Proved here (LEAN BANK)

* `branchClassBound_zero` — the zero functional satisfies every `BranchClassBound` (vacuity: the
  field constrains nothing while `D0` is uninterpreted);
* `branchClassBound_of_uniform` — the generic composition step "linear functional + a uniform
  eventual bound on every source-factorized weight ⟹ `BranchClassBound`";
* `zero_frequency_eventually_le` — the V25 localized bound, re-packaged: for every `A`, eventually
  `‖FullSum‖ ≤ √(Σ τ_J) √(C₁ Bnd/log^A) + C₂ MN/log^A` (direct reuse of
  `zero_frequency_localized_bound`, no new estimate).
-/

namespace Erdos287
namespace ResearchBankV29
namespace ZeroBranchComposition

open ResearchBankV22.IndependentFactorization ResearchBankV28.RepairedAnalyticBundle
open ResearchBankV25.LocalizationContract ResearchBankV25.CorrectionAggregation

/-- **Zero functional is a branch class bound** (LEAN BANK; vacuity witness). -/
theorem branchClassBound_zero (Us Ur : ℕ → ℕ → Finset ℕ) :
    BranchClassBound Us Ur (fun _ _ => 0) :=
  ⟨fun _ _ _ _ _ => by simp, fun _ _ hε => ⟨0, fun _ _ _ _ => by simpa using hε.le⟩⟩

/-- **Generic branch composition step** (LEAN BANK). -/
theorem branchClassBound_of_uniform {Us Ur : ℕ → ℕ → Finset ℕ} {DEb : ℕ → (Finset ℕ → ℝ) → ℝ}
    (hlin : ∀ M {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] (c : ι → ℝ) (g : ι → Finset ℕ → ℝ),
      DEb M (fun A => ∑ i, c i * g i A) = ∑ i, c i * DEb M (g i))
    (bound : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ) (hb : ∀ S M g, SourceFactorization g (Us S M) (Ur S M) → |DEb M g| ≤ bound S M)
    (hsmall : ∀ S, ∀ ε > 0, ∃ M₀ : ℕ, ∀ M ≥ M₀, bound S M ≤ ε) :
    BranchClassBound Us Ur DEb := by
  refine ⟨hlin, fun S ε hε => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨M₀, hM₀⟩ := hsmall S ε hε
  exact ⟨M₀, fun M hM g hg => (hb S M g hg).trans (hM₀ M hM)⟩

/-- **V25 zero-frequency bound, re-packaged** (LEAN CONDITIONAL on the V25 `BDHEnergyProvider`
and `MaskedSWProvider`; direct reuse). -/
theorem zero_frequency_eventually_le {f : ℕ} [NeZero f] {c : ℤ} {J : ℕ} (Z : ZeroFreqData f c J)
    {Bnd MN : ℝ → ℝ} (hB : BDHEnergyProvider f J Z.Ns Z.γ Z.U Bnd)
    (hM : MaskedSWProvider f c J Z.Qs Z.Ns Z.γ MN) (A : ℕ) :
    ∃ C₁ C₂ : ℝ, 0 ≤ C₁ ∧ 0 ≤ C₂ ∧ ∃ x0 : ℝ, ∀ x ≥ x0,
      ‖FullSum f (Z.Qs x) (Z.κ x) (Z.rq x) (Z.Ns x) (Z.γ x)‖ ≤
        Real.sqrt (∑ q ∈ Z.Qs x, tauJ J q) * Real.sqrt (C₁ * Bnd x / Real.log x ^ A) +
          C₂ * MN x / Real.log x ^ A :=
  zero_frequency_localized_bound Z hB hM A

end ZeroBranchComposition
end ResearchBankV29
end Erdos287

import Mathlib.Tactic

/-!
# Erdős #287 — Research Bank V7: bounded adaptive absorption (exact finite charging)

INTERNAL #287 RESEARCH PROGRAMME ONLY.  **Erdős #287 is `OPEN` here and is not claimed.**

This module is pure finite combinatorics: every theorem is kernel-proved, with no external input.
It formalizes the **charging theorem** underlying bounded adaptive absorption.

Setting (all finite).  `Z0` is the current zero set, `G0` the set of fixed-one guards, `W` the
family of absorbed rows, and `U ⊆ W` the sub-family of rows that are actually *used* for
branching.  Each charged row is charged either to a zero of `Z0` (at most **two** rows per zero)
or to a guard of `G0` (at most **one** row per guard); at most a `3γ`-fraction of the rows escapes
charging.  The conclusions are the exact finite bounds

* `(1 - 3γ) |W| ≤ 2|Z₀| + |G₀|`  (guarded form),
* `(1 - 3γ) |W| ≤ 2|Z₀|`         (unguarded form, `G₀ = ∅`),

and for the canonical choice `γ = 1/8`

* `|W| ≤ (16/5)|Z₀| + (8/5)|G₀|`,   `|U| ≤ (2/5)|Z₀| + (1/5)|G₀|`,
* `|W| ≤ (16/5)|Z₀|`,               `|U| ≤ (2/5)|Z₀|`.

A branching-bit budget (`branching_bits_le`) is banked in the same finite form.

**Scope firewall.**  Nothing here asserts that any absorbed row family or row completion *exists*:
the asymptotic existence of row completions is deliberately *not* encoded in these finite charging
lemmas (see `charging_does_not_give_existence`).
-/

namespace Erdos287
namespace ResearchBankV7
namespace Absorption

open Finset

/-! ## 1.  The finite fibre-counting kernel -/

/-- If `f` maps `s` into `t` and every fibre over `t` has at most `n` elements, then
`|s| ≤ n |t|`. -/
theorem card_le_of_fibre_bound {s t : Finset ℕ} {f : ℕ → ℕ} {n : ℕ}
    (hmaps : ∀ a ∈ s, f a ∈ t) (hfib : ∀ b ∈ t, {a ∈ s | f a = b}.card ≤ n) :
    s.card ≤ n * t.card := by
  have himg : s.image f ⊆ t := by
    intro b hb
    obtain ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hb
    exact hmaps a ha
  have h1 : s.card ≤ n * (s.image f).card :=
    Finset.card_le_mul_card_image s n (fun b hb => hfib b (himg hb))
  exact h1.trans (Nat.mul_le_mul_left n (Finset.card_le_card himg))

/-! ## 2.  Guarded charging data -/

/-- The exact finite hypotheses of the adaptive-absorption charging argument.

`W` is the absorbed row family, `Z0` the current zero set, `G0` the fixed-one guard set.  Rows in
`chargedZ` are charged to zeros (at most two per zero), rows in `chargedG` to guards (at most one
per guard); `gamma` bounds the fraction of rows that escape charging. -/
structure ChargingData where
  /-- The current zero set. -/
  Z0 : Finset ℕ
  /-- The fixed-one guard set (empty in the unguarded regime). -/
  G0 : Finset ℕ
  /-- The absorbed row family. -/
  W : Finset ℕ
  /-- The rows charged to zeros. -/
  chargedZ : Finset ℕ
  /-- The rows charged to guards. -/
  chargedG : Finset ℕ
  /-- The charging map to zeros. -/
  siteZ : ℕ → ℕ
  /-- The charging map to guards. -/
  siteG : ℕ → ℕ
  /-- Charged rows are rows. -/
  chargedZ_sub : chargedZ ⊆ W
  /-- Charged rows are rows. -/
  chargedG_sub : chargedG ⊆ W
  /-- The zero-charging map lands in the zero set. -/
  siteZ_maps : ∀ r ∈ chargedZ, siteZ r ∈ Z0
  /-- The guard-charging map lands in the guard set. -/
  siteG_maps : ∀ r ∈ chargedG, siteG r ∈ G0
  /-- **Two rows per zero.** -/
  siteZ_fibre : ∀ z ∈ Z0, {r ∈ chargedZ | siteZ r = z}.card ≤ 2
  /-- **One row per fixed-one guard.** -/
  siteG_fibre : ∀ g ∈ G0, {r ∈ chargedG | siteG r = g}.card ≤ 1
  /-- The escape fraction parameter. -/
  gamma : ℚ
  /-- At most a `3γ`-fraction of the absorbed rows escapes charging. -/
  escape : (W.card : ℚ) - (chargedZ.card + chargedG.card) ≤ 3 * gamma * W.card

/-- Rows charged to zeros are at most twice the number of zeros. -/
theorem chargedZ_card_le (c : ChargingData) : c.chargedZ.card ≤ 2 * c.Z0.card :=
  card_le_of_fibre_bound c.siteZ_maps c.siteZ_fibre

/-- Rows charged to guards are at most the number of guards. -/
theorem chargedG_card_le (c : ChargingData) : c.chargedG.card ≤ c.G0.card := by
  have := card_le_of_fibre_bound c.siteG_maps c.siteG_fibre
  simpa using this

/-! ## 3.  The guarded charging inequality -/

/-- **Guarded charging theorem (kernel).**  `(1 − 3γ)·|W| ≤ 2·z₀ + g₀`. -/
theorem guarded_charging (c : ChargingData) :
    (1 - 3 * c.gamma) * (c.W.card : ℚ) ≤ 2 * c.Z0.card + c.G0.card := by
  have hZ : (c.chargedZ.card : ℚ) ≤ 2 * c.Z0.card := by exact_mod_cast chargedZ_card_le c
  have hG : (c.chargedG.card : ℚ) ≤ c.G0.card := by exact_mod_cast chargedG_card_le c
  have h := c.escape
  nlinarith [h, hZ, hG]

/-- **Unguarded charging theorem (kernel).**  With no fixed-one guards, `(1 − 3γ)·W ≤ 2|Z₀|`. -/
theorem unguarded_charging (c : ChargingData) (hG : c.G0 = ∅) :
    (1 - 3 * c.gamma) * (c.W.card : ℚ) ≤ 2 * c.Z0.card := by
  have := guarded_charging c
  rw [hG] at this
  simpa using this

/-! ## 4.  The canonical choice `γ = 1/8` -/

/-- **Guarded budget at `γ = 1/8`.**  `|W| ≤ (16/5) z₀ + (8/5) g₀`. -/
theorem guarded_W_bound (c : ChargingData) (hγ : c.gamma = 1/8) :
    (c.W.card : ℚ) ≤ (16/5) * c.Z0.card + (8/5) * c.G0.card := by
  have h := guarded_charging c
  rw [hγ] at h
  linarith

/-- **Guarded branching budget at `γ = 1/8`.**  If the used family satisfies `|U| ≤ γ|W|`, then
`|U| ≤ (2/5) z₀ + (1/5) g₀`. -/
theorem guarded_U_bound (c : ChargingData) (hγ : c.gamma = 1/8) {U : Finset ℕ}
    (hU : (U.card : ℚ) ≤ c.gamma * c.W.card) :
    (U.card : ℚ) ≤ (2/5) * c.Z0.card + (1/5) * c.G0.card := by
  have hW := guarded_W_bound c hγ
  rw [hγ] at hU
  linarith

/-- **Unguarded budget at `γ = 1/8`.**  `|W| ≤ (16/5)|Z₀|`. -/
theorem unguarded_W_bound (c : ChargingData) (hγ : c.gamma = 1/8) (hG : c.G0 = ∅) :
    (c.W.card : ℚ) ≤ (16/5) * c.Z0.card := by
  have h := unguarded_charging c hG
  rw [hγ] at h
  linarith

/-- **Unguarded branching budget at `γ = 1/8`.**  `|U| ≤ (2/5)|Z₀|`. -/
theorem unguarded_U_bound (c : ChargingData) (hγ : c.gamma = 1/8) (hG : c.G0 = ∅) {U : Finset ℕ}
    (hU : (U.card : ℚ) ≤ c.gamma * c.W.card) :
    (U.card : ℚ) ≤ (2/5) * c.Z0.card := by
  have hW := unguarded_W_bound c hγ hG
  rw [hγ] at hU
  linarith

/-! ## 5.  Branching-bit budget -/

/-- **Branching-bit budget (kernel).**  If every absorbed row contributes at most `b` branching
bits, the whole absorption tree spends at most `b·((16/5) z₀ + (8/5) g₀)` bits. -/
theorem branching_bits_le (c : ChargingData) (hγ : c.gamma = 1/8) (b : ℕ) (bits : ℚ)
    (hbits : bits ≤ b * c.W.card) :
    bits ≤ (b : ℚ) * ((16/5) * c.Z0.card + (8/5) * c.G0.card) := by
  have hW := guarded_W_bound c hγ
  have hb : (0:ℚ) ≤ (b : ℚ) := by positivity
  nlinarith [hW, hbits, hb]

/-! ## 6.  Scope firewall -/

/-- **Firewall.**  The finite charging theorems are bounds *given* a charging datum; they do not
assert that any absorbed row family, row completion or zero set exists.  Formally, a universally
quantified implication never inhabits its own hypothesis. -/
theorem charging_does_not_give_existence :
    ¬ ∀ (H C : ChargingData → Prop), (∀ c, H c → C c) → ∃ c, H c := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := h (fun _ => False) (fun _ => True) (fun _ h => h.elim)
  exact hc

/-- **Firewall.**  A bound on `|W|` in terms of `|Z₀|` is vacuous when the configuration does not
exist: with an empty zero set and empty row family every budget above is satisfied, and no
completion has been produced. -/
theorem trivial_charging_datum_exists :
    ∃ c : ChargingData, c.Z0 = ∅ ∧ c.W = ∅ ∧ c.gamma = 1/8 :=
  ⟨{ Z0 := ∅, G0 := ∅, W := ∅, chargedZ := ∅, chargedG := ∅,
     siteZ := id, siteG := id,
     chargedZ_sub := by simp, chargedG_sub := by simp,
     siteZ_maps := by simp, siteG_maps := by simp,
     siteZ_fibre := by simp, siteG_fibre := by simp,
     gamma := 1/8, escape := by norm_num }, rfl, rfl, rfl⟩

end Absorption
end ResearchBankV7
end Erdos287

@@BEGIN_FILE bytes=6172 sha256=2cc9f170e43a0b36ebb93f9059f1bb55858db61fc30ff2cf07ab7b7d2f7c424b path=LEAN_PROJECT/RequestProject/Erdos287/ResearchBankV7/Epochs.lean@@
import Mathlib.Tactic

/-!
# Erdős #287 — Research Bank V7: research epochs and meta-firewalls

INTERNAL #287 RESEARCH PROGRAMME ONLY.  **Erdős #287 is `OPEN` here and is not claimed.**

V7 is a strictly **append-only** layer: nothing of `AnchoredV2/V3/V4`, `ResearchBankV5` or
`ResearchBankV6` is edited, renamed, moved, weakened or reinterpreted.  This module introduces the
*chronology* that makes the older ledgers and the current ledger simultaneously readable:

* `Epoch` — the four research epochs (V6 upper-gap/carry, STABLE-ENTRY, exact-HIT / arithmetic
  spine, current ENTRY-FIRST);
* `OwnerRecord` — an epoch-stamped owner row carrying an actual `Prop` claim;
* meta-firewalls (all machine-checked):
  - `superseded_does_not_mean_false`,
  - `historical_open_does_not_determine_current_owner`,
  - `later_reduction_does_not_inhabit_earlier_owner`,
  - `no_closure_propagation_through_ledger_edges`.

None of these is a mathematical statement about #287: they are exact statements about the
bookkeeping calculus, proved so that "current owner" talk cannot silently contradict an earlier
historical ledger.
-/

namespace Erdos287
namespace ResearchBankV7
namespace Epochs

/-! ## 1.  The epochs -/

/-- The research epochs of the #287 programme after V6. -/
inductive Epoch
  /-- The V6 upper-gap / carry epoch (row mass, carry identity, height aggregation). -/
  | v6UpperGapCarry
  /-- The STABLE-ENTRY epoch (seed traces, bounded adaptive absorption trees). -/
  | stableEntry
  /-- The exact-HIT / arithmetic-spine epoch (interval lifting, spine certificates, erasure). -/
  | exactHitSpine
  /-- The current ENTRY-FIRST epoch. -/
  | entryFirst
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Chronological index of an epoch. -/
def Epoch.index : Epoch → ℕ
  | .v6UpperGapCarry => 0
  | .stableEntry => 1
  | .exactHitSpine => 2
  | .entryFirst => 3

/-- The chronology is injective: epochs are pairwise distinct stages. -/
theorem epoch_index_injective : Function.Injective Epoch.index := by
  intro a b h; cases a <;> cases b <;> simp_all [Epoch.index]

/-- The four epochs occur in the recorded order. -/
theorem epoch_chronology :
    Epoch.v6UpperGapCarry.index < Epoch.stableEntry.index ∧
    Epoch.stableEntry.index < Epoch.exactHitSpine.index ∧
    Epoch.exactHitSpine.index < Epoch.entryFirst.index := by decide

/-- The current epoch. -/
def currentEpoch : Epoch := Epoch.entryFirst

/-- Every epoch is at most the current one. -/
theorem le_currentEpoch (e : Epoch) : e.index ≤ currentEpoch.index := by
  cases e <;> decide

/-! ## 2.  Epoch-stamped owner records -/

/-- The lifecycle flag of an owner *inside its own epoch*. -/
inductive OwnerFlag
  /-- Unresolved in its epoch and still unresolved now. -/
  | openOwner
  /-- Bypassed or refined by later work.  **Never** means "false". -/
  | superseded
  /-- Discharged at its stated scope. -/
  | discharged
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- An epoch-stamped owner row.  The `claim` field is an actual `Prop`; a row is *data*, so
creating a row never inhabits `claim`. -/
structure OwnerRecord where
  /-- Human-readable owner name. -/
  name : String
  /-- The epoch in which this owner was the current one. -/
  epoch : Epoch
  /-- The mathematical claim of the owner. -/
  claim : Prop
  /-- Its lifecycle flag. -/
  flag : OwnerFlag

/-! ## 3.  Meta-firewalls -/

/-- **Firewall: `superseded` does not mean `false`.**  There is a `superseded` owner record whose
claim is true; being bypassed by later work is a statement about the *architecture*, never a
refutation of the statement. -/
theorem superseded_does_not_mean_false :
    ∃ r : OwnerRecord, r.flag = OwnerFlag.superseded ∧ r.claim :=
  ⟨{ name := "superseded probe", epoch := Epoch.v6UpperGapCarry, claim := True,
     flag := OwnerFlag.superseded }, rfl, trivial⟩

/-- **Firewall: the `superseded` flag is truth-neutral.**  Both a true and a false claim can carry
it, so the flag transports no truth value in either direction. -/
theorem superseded_flag_is_truth_neutral :
    (∃ r : OwnerRecord, r.flag = OwnerFlag.superseded ∧ r.claim) ∧
    (∃ r : OwnerRecord, r.flag = OwnerFlag.superseded ∧ ¬ r.claim) :=
  ⟨superseded_does_not_mean_false,
   ⟨{ name := "superseded false probe", epoch := Epoch.v6UpperGapCarry, claim := False,
      flag := OwnerFlag.superseded }, rfl, not_false⟩⟩

/-- **Firewall: a historical owner being open does not say that the current owner is the same
statement.**  Openness of one proposition transports nothing to another proposition. -/
theorem historical_open_does_not_determine_current_owner :
    ¬ ∀ P Q : Prop, ¬ P → ¬ Q := by
  intro h
  exact (h False True not_false) trivial

/-- The same, in record form: two owners of different epochs may carry genuinely different
claims, one unprovable and one provable. -/
theorem owners_of_distinct_epochs_may_differ :
    ∃ r s : OwnerRecord, r.epoch ≠ s.epoch ∧ ¬ r.claim ∧ s.claim :=
  ⟨{ name := "historical owner", epoch := Epoch.v6UpperGapCarry, claim := False,
     flag := OwnerFlag.superseded },
   { name := "current owner probe", epoch := Epoch.entryFirst, claim := True,
     flag := OwnerFlag.openOwner },
   by decide, not_false, trivial⟩

/-- **Firewall: a later reduction does not retroactively inhabit an earlier open proposition.**
From `Q → P` (a later statement reducing to the earlier owner `P`) one may not conclude `P`. -/
theorem later_reduction_does_not_inhabit_earlier_owner :
    ¬ ∀ P Q : Prop, (Q → P) → P := by
  intro h
  exact h False False id

/-- **Firewall: no closure status propagates merely through ledger edges.**  An edge `P → Q`
together with a proof of `Q` never yields `P`. -/
theorem no_closure_propagation_through_ledger_edges :
    ¬ ∀ P Q : Prop, (P → Q) → Q → P := by
  intro h
  exact h False True (fun x => x.elim) trivial

/-- **Firewall: edges compose, statuses do not.**  Composing two proved edges is legitimate
(kernel), but that is the *only* thing an edge does. -/
theorem edges_compose {P Q R : Prop} (h₁ : P → Q) (h₂ : Q → R) : P → R := fun p => h₂ (h₁ p)

end Epochs
end ResearchBankV7
end Erdos287

@@END_FILE@@
@@BEGIN_FILE bytes=5713 sha256=0550084889a07dae6cb30a22ea0ec564a6fcd7b33eb715934b1053835ccea211 path=LEAN_PROJECT/RequestProject/Erdos287/ResearchBankV7/ErasureHit.lean@@
import RequestProject.Erdos287.ResearchBankV7.Spine

/-!
# Erdős #287 — Research Bank V7: ERASURE-HIT (exact robustness of a certified spine)

INTERNAL #287 RESEARCH PROGRAMME ONLY.  **Erdős #287 is `OPEN` here and is not claimed.**

Exact rational/integer robustness statement.  If a certified spine `𝒫` lies inside an intermediate
support, `𝒫 ⊆ T' ⊆ T`, then the certified lattice interval survives **any** treatment of the
remaining non-spine coordinates:

* `erasure_hit` — every certified lattice value is still hit by a subset of `T'` whose support is
  contained in the spine, i.e. all non-spine coordinates are erased (set to `0`);
* `erasure_hit_with_fixed_part` — if an arbitrary non-spine part `F ⊆ T' \ 𝒫` is instead fixed to
  `1`, the whole certified interval is hit *translated by the mass of `F`*, again exactly;
* `erasure_hit_complement` — the two-sided form.  Writing `W = ∑_{n ∈ T'} w n` for the total
  weight, if `g ∣ W` and the certified interval reaches at least half of the total weight
  (`W ≤ 2B`, the exact overlap condition), then **every** lattice point of `[A, W − A]` is an
  exact subset weight of `T'`.  In `J`-numerator units with `w n = J/n` this is precisely
  `[α, ∑_{n ∈ T'} 1/n − α] ∩ (1/J)ℤ`.
* `erasure_hit_rational` — the same statement in rational mass language.

**Terminology firewall.**  As in `IntervalLifting`, a failed overlap condition means the
certificate does not apply; it is *not* an UNSAT statement (`overlap_failure_is_not_unsat`).
-/

namespace Erdos287
namespace ResearchBankV7
namespace ErasureHit

open Finset IntervalLifting

/-! ## 1.  Erasing the non-spine coordinates -/

/-- **ERASURE-HIT (kernel).**  For `𝒫 ⊆ T'`, every value of the certified lattice interval is
still reached inside `T'`, by a subset of the spine: all remaining non-spine coordinates are
erased to `0`. -/
theorem erasure_hit {w : ℕ → ℤ} {P T' : Finset ℕ} {g A B : ℤ} (hPT : P ⊆ T')
    (hP : ReachesLattice w P g A B) :
    ∀ n : ℤ, g ∣ n → A ≤ n → n ≤ B → ∃ S, S ⊆ P ∧ S ⊆ T' ∧ ∑ x ∈ S, w x = n := by
  intro n hg hA hB
  obtain ⟨S, hS, hsum⟩ := hP n hg hA hB
  exact ⟨S, hS, hS.trans hPT, hsum⟩

/-- **ERASURE-HIT with an arbitrary fixed part (kernel).**  If the non-spine coordinates are not
erased but an arbitrary part `F` of them is fixed to `1`, the reachable values of `T'` contain the
certified interval translated by the weight of `F`, exactly. -/
theorem erasure_hit_with_fixed_part {w : ℕ → ℤ} {P T' F : Finset ℕ} {g A B : ℤ}
    (hPT : P ⊆ T') (hF : F ⊆ T' \ P) (hP : ReachesLattice w P g A B) :
    ∀ n : ℤ, g ∣ n → A ≤ n → n ≤ B →
      ∃ S ⊆ T', ∑ x ∈ S, w x = n + ∑ x ∈ F, w x := by
  intro n hg hA hB
  obtain ⟨S, hS, hsum⟩ := hP n hg hA hB
  have hdisj : Disjoint S F := by
    refine Finset.disjoint_left.2 ?_
    intro a haS haF
    exact (Finset.mem_sdiff.1 (hF haF)).2 (hS haS)
  refine ⟨S ∪ F, Finset.union_subset (hS.trans hPT) (hF.trans Finset.sdiff_subset), ?_⟩
  rw [Finset.sum_union hdisj, hsum]

/-! ## 2.  The two-sided (complement) form -/

/-- **ERASURE-HIT, two-sided (kernel).**  Let `W = ∑_{x ∈ T'} w x`.  If the certified spine
interval `[A, B]` satisfies the exact overlap condition `W ≤ 2B` and `g ∣ W`, then every lattice
point of `[A, W − A]` is an exact subset weight of `T'`. -/
theorem erasure_hit_complement {w : ℕ → ℤ} {P T' : Finset ℕ} {g A B : ℤ} (hPT : P ⊆ T')
    (hP : ReachesLattice w P g A B) (hW : g ∣ ∑ x ∈ T', w x)
    (hover : ∑ x ∈ T', w x ≤ 2 * B) :
    ReachesLattice w T' g A (∑ x ∈ T', w x - A) := by
  classical
  set W : ℤ := ∑ x ∈ T', w x with hWdef
  intro n hg hA hB
  by_cases hnB : n ≤ B
  · exact (hP.mono hPT) n hg hA hnB
  · push_neg at hnB
    have hgm : g ∣ W - n := dvd_sub hW hg
    obtain ⟨S, hS, hsum⟩ := hP (W - n) hgm (by omega) (by omega)
    refine ⟨T' \ S, Finset.sdiff_subset, ?_⟩
    rw [Finset.sum_sdiff_eq_sub (hS.trans hPT), hsum, ← hWdef]
    ring

/-! ## 3.  Rational mass form -/

/-- **ERASURE-HIT in rational mass language.**  With `w n = J / n` for denominators dividing `J`,
a certified lattice value `k` corresponds to the rational mass `k / J`; the statement above says
that every rational of the form `k/J` in the certified window is an exact subset mass of `T'`. -/
theorem erasure_hit_rational {w : ℕ → ℤ} {P T' : Finset ℕ} {g A B : ℤ} {J : ℕ} (hJ : 0 < J)
    (f : ℕ → ℚ) (hf : ∀ x, f x = (w x : ℚ) / J)
    (hPT : P ⊆ T') (hP : ReachesLattice w P g A B) :
    ∀ k : ℤ, g ∣ k → A ≤ k → k ≤ B →
      ∃ S ⊆ T', ∑ x ∈ S, f x = (k : ℚ) / J := by
  intro k hg hA hB
  obtain ⟨S, hSP, hST, hsum⟩ := erasure_hit hPT hP k hg hA hB
  refine ⟨S, hST, ?_⟩
  have hJ' : (J : ℚ) ≠ 0 := by positivity
  calc ∑ x ∈ S, f x = ∑ x ∈ S, ((w x : ℚ) / J) := Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun x _ => hf x)
    _ = (∑ x ∈ S, (w x : ℚ)) / J := by rw [Finset.sum_div]
    _ = (k : ℚ) / J := by rw [← Int.cast_sum, hsum]

/-! ## 4.  Terminology firewall -/

/-- **Firewall.**  A violated overlap condition (`2B < W`) only means that the two-sided form does
not apply; the one-sided certified interval is untouched and nothing is unsatisfiable. -/
theorem overlap_failure_is_not_unsat :
    ∃ (w : ℕ → ℤ) (P T' : Finset ℕ) (g A B : ℤ),
      P ⊆ T' ∧ ReachesLattice w P g A B ∧ 2 * B < ∑ x ∈ T', w x := by
  refine ⟨fun _ => 10, ∅, {1, 2}, 1, 0, 0, by simp, ?_, by decide⟩
  intro n _ hA hB
  exact ⟨∅, by simp, by simp; omega⟩

end ErasureHit
end ResearchBankV7
end Erdos287

@@END_FILE@@
@@BEGIN_FILE bytes=5949 sha256=e10566ec4c06e620d4583a3e986aac807c65c9fb019a44e01304174c42e4c700 path=LEAN_PROJECT/RequestProject/Erdos287/ResearchBankV7/FiniteSourceKills.lean@@
import RequestProject.Erdos287.Blocker

/-!
# Erdős #287 — Research Bank V7: finite whole-source contradictions as diagnostics

INTERNAL #287 RESEARCH PROGRAMME ONLY.  **Erdős #287 is `OPEN` here and is not claimed.**

Exact, fully verified **finite** source contradictions of the `p = 2q ± 1` pattern, obtained from
the banked necessary row/exclusion equations together with the no-`00` (gap-`≤ 2`) rule.  Each is a
statement about one explicit finite window, classified `FINITE-SOURCE-KILL`; the failure of the
pattern at a particular prime is classified `COUNTERFIXTURE`.

* `sourceKill_2q_add_one` / `sourceKill_2q_sub_one` — the two general patterns;
* `sourceKill_59`, `sourceKill_83`, `sourceKill_107` — kills of the `p = 2q + 1` pattern;
* `sourceKill_61`, `sourceKill_73` — kills of the `p = 2q − 1` pattern;
* `kill_pattern_not_universal` — COUNTERFIXTURE: the pattern is not available at every prime;
* `finite_kill_does_not_give_uniform_supply` — the meta-firewall demanded by the discipline: a
  finite source kill is **not** an asymptotic theorem and does not supply the prime-pair pattern
  uniformly (the supply statement `SafePrimeSupply` is itself recorded as an open external input).
-/

namespace Erdos287
namespace ResearchBankV7
namespace FiniteSourceKills

open Erdos287

/-! ## 1.  The two general finite-kill patterns -/

/-- **FINITE-SOURCE-KILL (`p = 2q + 1`).**  If a gap-`≤ 2` counterexample has a prime
`p = 2q + 1` with `q` prime, `q > 25 = C(4)`, inside the top window `(M/2, M] ∩ (N, M]`, the
source dies: `p − 1 = 2q` is a hole by prime-power window exclusion and `p` is a hole by the
large-prime exclusion, giving two adjacent holes. -/
theorem sourceKill_2q_add_one (ce : Gap2CE) {p q : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hq : q.Prime)
    (hpN : ce.N + 1 ≤ p) (hpM : p ≤ ce.M) (hM2 : ce.M < 2 * p)
    (heq : p = 2 * q + 1) (hq25 : 25 < q) : False :=
  ce.safePrime_blocker hp hq hpN hpM hM2 heq hq25

/-- **FINITE-SOURCE-KILL (`p = 2q − 1`).**  The mirrored pattern: `p + 1 = 2q` with `q` prime,
`q > 25 = C(4)`, `p` prime in the top window. -/
theorem sourceKill_2q_sub_one (ce : Gap2CE) {p q : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hq : q.Prime)
    (hpN : ce.N ≤ p) (hpM : p + 1 ≤ ce.M) (hM2 : ce.M < 2 * p)
    (heq : p + 1 = 2 * q) (hq25 : 25 < q) : False := by
  refine ce.goodPrime_blocker_add (p := p) (d := 2) (r := q) (e := 1) hp hq le_rfl (by norm_num)
    hpN hpM hM2 (by simpa using heq) ?_
  have h4 : (2 * 2 : ℕ) = 4 := by norm_num
  rw [h4, C_four]
  exact_mod_cast hq25

/-! ## 2.  Explicit checked instances -/

/-- **FINITE-SOURCE-KILL.**  `p = 59 = 2·29 + 1`: no gap-`≤ 2` counterexample has
`N < 59 ≤ M < 118`. -/
theorem sourceKill_59 (ce : Gap2CE) (hN : ce.N < 59) (hM : 59 ≤ ce.M) (hM2 : ce.M < 118) :
    False :=
  sourceKill_2q_add_one ce (p := 59) (q := 29) (by norm_num) (by norm_num) (by omega) hM
    (by omega) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)

/-- **FINITE-SOURCE-KILL.**  `p = 83 = 2·41 + 1`. -/
theorem sourceKill_83 (ce : Gap2CE) (hN : ce.N < 83) (hM : 83 ≤ ce.M) (hM2 : ce.M < 166) :
    False :=
  sourceKill_2q_add_one ce (p := 83) (q := 41) (by norm_num) (by norm_num) (by omega) hM
    (by omega) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)

/-- **FINITE-SOURCE-KILL.**  `p = 107 = 2·53 + 1`. -/
theorem sourceKill_107 (ce : Gap2CE) (hN : ce.N < 107) (hM : 107 ≤ ce.M) (hM2 : ce.M < 214) :
    False :=
  sourceKill_2q_add_one ce (p := 107) (q := 53) (by norm_num) (by norm_num) (by omega) hM
    (by omega) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)

/-- **FINITE-SOURCE-KILL.**  `p = 61 = 2·31 − 1`. -/
theorem sourceKill_61 (ce : Gap2CE) (hN : ce.N ≤ 61) (hM : 62 ≤ ce.M) (hM2 : ce.M < 122) :
    False :=
  sourceKill_2q_sub_one ce (p := 61) (q := 31) (by norm_num) (by norm_num) hN hM (by omega)
    (by norm_num) (by norm_num)

/-- **FINITE-SOURCE-KILL.**  `p = 73 = 2·37 − 1`. -/
theorem sourceKill_73 (ce : Gap2CE) (hN : ce.N ≤ 73) (hM : 74 ≤ ce.M) (hM2 : ce.M < 146) :
    False :=
  sourceKill_2q_sub_one ce (p := 73) (q := 37) (by norm_num) (by norm_num) hN hM (by omega)
    (by norm_num) (by norm_num)

/-! ## 3.  Counterfixture and supply firewall -/

/-- **COUNTERFIXTURE.**  The `p = 2q ± 1` kill pattern is *not* available at every prime of the
top window: at `p = 53` neither `(p − 1)/2 = 26` nor `(p + 1)/2 = 27` is a prime exceeding
`C(4) = 25`. -/
theorem kill_pattern_not_universal :
    ¬ (∃ q : ℕ, q.Prime ∧ 25 < q ∧ (53 = 2 * q + 1 ∨ 53 + 1 = 2 * q)) := by
  rintro ⟨q, hq, h25, h | h⟩
  · have : q = 26 := by omega
    subst this
    exact absurd hq (by norm_num)
  · have : q = 27 := by omega
    subst this
    exact absurd hq (by norm_num)

/-- **OPEN EXTERNAL INPUT (uninhabited here).**  The uniform supply statement that the kill pattern
would need in order to become an asymptotic theorem: every large window contains a prime
`p ∈ (M/2, M]` of the `p = 2q ± 1` shape with `q` prime.  This is an open problem of the
Sophie-Germain circle and is **not** proved anywhere in this project. -/
def SafePrimeSupply : Prop :=
  ∀ M : ℕ, 100 ≤ M → ∃ p q : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ q.Prime ∧ 25 < q ∧
    (p = 2 * q + 1 ∨ p + 1 = 2 * q) ∧ M < 2 * p ∧ p ≤ M

/-- **Meta-firewall.**  Finitely many verified source kills do not supply the prime-pair pattern
uniformly: from statements about finitely many explicit windows nothing follows for all windows. -/
theorem finite_kill_does_not_give_uniform_supply :
    ¬ ∀ P : ℕ → Prop, (P 59 ∧ P 83 ∧ P 107) → ∀ n, P n := by
  intro h
  have := h (fun n => n ≠ 0) ⟨by norm_num, by norm_num, by norm_num⟩ 0
  exact this rfl

/-- **Meta-firewall.**  A finite source kill is a diagnostic about one window, never an asymptotic
theorem: it does not inhabit `SafePrimeSupply`. -/
theorem finite_kills_do_not_inhabit_supply :
    ¬ ∀ P Q : Prop, P → Q := by
  intro h
  exact h True False trivial

end FiniteSourceKills
end ResearchBankV7
end Erdos287

@@END_FILE@@

import Mathlib.Tactic

/-!
# Erdős #287 — Research Bank V7: Fouvry-pin localization at its true evidence level

INTERNAL #287 RESEARCH PROGRAMME ONLY.  **Erdős #287 is `OPEN` here and is not claimed.**

The Fouvry lane rests on analytic ingredients that are **not** formalized in this project.  They
are recorded here as explicit, *uninhabited* external interfaces:

* `FouvryShiftedPrimeInput` (Fouvry / Luca–Young shifted-prime divisor input);
* `SelbergUpperBoundSieve`;
* `BrunTitchmarsh`;
* `PrimeCountingEstimate`.

Everything derived from them is stated as an implication with the external premise visible
(`CONDITIONAL-BANKED`), and the finite/arithmetic consequences are kernel-proved:

* `pin_capture_conditional` — the pin-capture inequality
  `Φ(𝓡) ≤ c·M·log(2H)/(log M)² + W(𝓡)/log(2H)`;
* `sublinear_support_cannot_capture_positive_proportion` — a sublinear-support residual family
  cannot contain a positive proportion of the pin population;
* `branch_budget_pin_localization` — the pin bound under the bounded-absorption branch budget.

Interpretation banked: Fouvry bulk is **no longer a separate completion owner** on a surviving
terminal leaf.  Firewall: none of this infers that a surviving terminal leaf exists
(`fouvry_bound_does_not_give_terminal_leaf`).
-/

namespace Erdos287
namespace ResearchBankV7
namespace FouvryPin

open Finset

/-! ## 1.  External analytic interfaces (uninhabited here) -/

/-- **EXTERNAL (uninhabited here).**  The Fouvry / Luca–Young shifted-prime input: for a positive
proportion of primes `p ≤ x`, the shifted prime `p − 1` has a divisor in a prescribed dyadic
range.  Not formalized in this project. -/
def FouvryShiftedPrimeInput : Prop :=
  ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ x : ℕ, 100 ≤ x → ∃ P : Finset ℕ,
    (∀ p ∈ P, p.Prime ∧ p ≤ x) ∧ δ * (x / Real.log x) ≤ (P.card : ℝ)

/-- **EXTERNAL (uninhabited here).**  A Selberg upper-bound sieve estimate for the sifted
quantities used in the pin lane.  Not formalized in this project. -/
def SelbergUpperBoundSieve (S : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ x z : ℕ, 2 ≤ z → z ≤ x → S x z ≤ c * (x / Real.log z)

/-- **EXTERNAL (uninhabited here).**  Brun–Titchmarsh: an upper bound for primes in an arithmetic
progression.  Not formalized in this project. -/
def BrunTitchmarsh (piAP : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ x q a : ℕ, 1 ≤ q → q < x →
    piAP x q a ≤ c * (x / ((q : ℝ) * Real.log (x / q)))

/-- **EXTERNAL (uninhabited here).**  The prime-counting estimate used for the pin population.
Not formalized in this project. -/
def PrimeCountingEstimate (pinPop : ℕ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ M : ℕ, 100 ≤ M → δ * (M / Real.log M) ≤ pinPop M

/-! ## 2.  The pin-capture inequality (conditional) -/

/-- The pin-capture inequality for a residual family `𝓡`, with pin count `Φ` and weight `W`:
`Φ(𝓡) ≤ c·M·log(2H)/(log M)² + W(𝓡)/log(2H)`. -/
def PinCaptureInequality (Phi W : Finset ℕ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ (M H : ℕ) (R : Finset ℕ), 100 ≤ M → 1 ≤ H →
    Phi R ≤ c * ((M : ℝ) * Real.log (2 * H) / (Real.log M) ^ 2)
      + W R / Real.log (2 * H)

/-- The adapter consuming the analytic inputs.  It is itself **external**: no Lean proof of it
exists in this project. -/
def PinCaptureAdapter (Phi W : Finset ℕ → ℝ) (S : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ) (piAP : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  FouvryShiftedPrimeInput ∧ SelbergUpperBoundSieve S ∧ BrunTitchmarsh piAP →
    PinCaptureInequality Phi W

/-- **CONDITIONAL-BANKED.**  The pin-capture inequality follows from the shifted-prime input, the
Selberg sieve and Brun–Titchmarsh through the adapter — and only that way. -/
theorem pin_capture_conditional {Phi W : Finset ℕ → ℝ} {S : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ} {piAP : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → ℝ}
    (hadapt : PinCaptureAdapter Phi W S piAP)
    (hF : FouvryShiftedPrimeInput) (hS : SelbergUpperBoundSieve S) (hBT : BrunTitchmarsh piAP) :
    PinCaptureInequality Phi W :=
  hadapt ⟨hF, hS, hBT⟩

/-- **CONDITIONAL-BANKED.**  The short-cofactor pin bound: the pin count of a residual family with
short cofactors is bounded by the capture inequality specialized at the family's own weight. -/
theorem short_cofactor_pin_bound {Phi W : Finset ℕ → ℝ} (h : PinCaptureInequality Phi W)
    (M H : ℕ) (R : Finset ℕ) (hM : 100 ≤ M) (hH : 1 ≤ H) :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ Phi R ≤ c * ((M : ℝ) * Real.log (2 * H) / (Real.log M) ^ 2)
      + W R / Real.log (2 * H) := by
  obtain ⟨c, hc, hineq⟩ := h
  exact ⟨c, hc, hineq M H R hM hH⟩

/-! ## 3.  Exact consequences of the inequality (kernel, given the inputs) -/

/-- **Kernel (given the numerical inputs).**  A residual family whose support weight is
sublinear cannot contain a positive proportion of the pin population: if the capture bound plus
the sublinear weight term stays below `ρ·pinPop`, the family's pin count does. -/
theorem sublinear_support_cannot_capture_positive_proportion
    {Phi : ℝ} {mainTerm weightTerm rho pinPop : ℝ}
    (hcap : Phi ≤ mainTerm + weightTerm)
    (hsub : mainTerm + weightTerm < rho * pinPop) :
    Phi < rho * pinPop :=
  lt_of_le_of_lt hcap hsub

/-- **Kernel (given the numerical inputs).**  Branch-budget pin localization: under the bounded
adaptive-absorption budget `W(𝓡) ≤ (16/5)z₀ + (8/5)g₀`, the pin-capture inequality localizes the
pin count in terms of the zero and guard budgets. -/
theorem branch_budget_pin_localization
    {Phi mainTerm weight L z0 g0 : ℝ} (hL : 0 < L)
    (hcap : Phi ≤ mainTerm + weight / L)
    (hbudget : weight ≤ (16/5) * z0 + (8/5) * g0) :
    Phi ≤ mainTerm + ((16/5) * z0 + (8/5) * g0) / L := by
  have hdiv : weight / L ≤ ((16/5) * z0 + (8/5) * g0) / L := by gcongr
  linarith

/-! ## 4.  Interpretation and firewalls -/

/-- **Interpretation (bookkeeping).**  On a surviving terminal leaf the Fouvry bulk is no longer a
separate completion owner: the pin bound is consumed inside the branch budget, which is what the
localization theorem above expresses.  This is recorded, not used as a mathematical premise. -/
def fouvryBulkNotSeparateOwner : String :=
  "Fouvry bulk is consumed by the branch budget; it is not a separate completion owner."

/-- **Firewall.**  No bound of this module infers the existence of a surviving terminal leaf: a
bound valid *on* a leaf never produces a leaf. -/
theorem fouvry_bound_does_not_give_terminal_leaf :
    ¬ ∀ (Leaf : Type) (H C : Leaf → Prop), (∀ l, H l → C l) → Nonempty Leaf := by
  intro h
  exact (h Empty (fun _ => True) (fun _ => True) (fun _ _ => trivial)).elim (fun e => e.elim)

/-- **Firewall.**  Conditional analytic records never become kernel theorems: an implication from
an uninhabited premise carries no conclusion. -/
theorem external_premise_does_not_upgrade :
    ¬ ∀ P Q : Prop, (P → Q) → Q := by
  intro h
  exact h False False id

end FouvryPin
end ResearchBankV7
end Erdos287

@@END_FILE@@
@@BEGIN_FILE bytes=8178 sha256=71b2b9734c56d0e7f139a01a26710abcbeaf710ba4400ae13f684999408b6d15 path=LEAN_PROJECT/RequestProject/Erdos287/ResearchBankV7/GuardedBranchHit.lean@@
import RequestProject.Erdos287.ResearchBankV7.ErasureHit

/-!
# Erdős #287 — Research Bank V7: the guarded branch-to-HIT theorem (conditional, exact)

INTERNAL #287 RESEARCH PROGRAMME ONLY.  **Erdős #287 is `OPEN` here and is not claimed.**

Exact rational theorem with an explicit hypothesis package.  Its inputs are

* a **genuine complete ENTRY reference word** `x₀`, represented by its actual selected support
  `T` (all denominators dividing the final modulus `J`) — never by a seed;
* a valid spine `𝒫 ⊆ T` with a certified reachable `J`-lattice interval `[A, B]`;
* compatible guards `G ⊆ T` (fixed ones) and a protected neutral set `Nprot ⊆ T`, both disjoint
  from the spine;
* an explicit zero budget `z`, with `|𝒫| ≤ z`;
* exact lower/upper mass margins `A ≤ w ≤ B` for the **actual deficit**
  `w = J·(S(x₀) − 1) = (∑_{n ∈ T} J/n) − J`.

Conclusion (`guarded_branch_to_hit`): the deficit is hit by an actual subset `S ⊆ 𝒫` of the
spine, so deleting `S` from the same physical branch — touching neither a guard nor a protected
neutral coordinate, and staying inside the zero budget — yields exactly `S = 1`.

Firewalls, machine-checked:

* `guarded_hit_does_not_give_entry_word` — the theorem does **not** produce a compatible ENTRY
  reference word;
* `guard_failure_does_not_kill_unguarded_branches` — failure of one fixed guarded construction
  does **not** refute unguarded ENTRY branches;
* `seed_mass_is_not_reference_mass` — a concrete counterfixture forbidding the substitution of the
  seed mass for `S(x₀)`.
-/

namespace Erdos287
namespace ResearchBankV7
namespace GuardedBranchHit

open Finset IntervalLifting

/-- The integer numerator weight of the denominator `n` at final modulus `J`. -/
def num (J n : ℕ) : ℤ := ((J / n : ℕ) : ℤ)

/-- For `n ∣ J` with `0 < n`, the numerator weight is the exact rational `J/n`. -/
theorem num_cast {J n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hdvd : n ∣ J) :
    ((num J n : ℤ) : ℚ) = (J : ℚ) / n := by
  have hn' : (n : ℚ) ≠ 0 := by positivity
  rw [num, Int.cast_natCast, Nat.cast_div hdvd hn']

/-- Exact conversion between rational subset mass and integer subset weight. -/
theorem mass_eq_weight_div {J : ℕ} (hJ : 0 < J) {S : Finset ℕ}
    (hS : ∀ n ∈ S, 0 < n ∧ n ∣ J) :
    ∑ n ∈ S, (1 : ℚ) / n = (∑ n ∈ S, (num J n : ℚ)) / J := by
  have hJ' : (J : ℚ) ≠ 0 := by positivity
  rw [Finset.sum_div]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
  intro n hn
  obtain ⟨hn0, hnd⟩ := hS n hn
  have hn' : (n : ℚ) ≠ 0 := by positivity
  rw [num_cast hn0 hnd]
  field_simp

/-- The complete hypothesis package of the guarded branch-to-HIT theorem. -/
structure GuardedBranch where
  /-- The final modulus. -/
  J : ℕ
  /-- Positivity of the final modulus. -/
  J_pos : 0 < J
  /-- The actual selected support of the complete ENTRY reference word `x₀`. -/
  T : Finset ℕ
  /-- Every selected denominator is positive and divides `J`. -/
  T_ok : ∀ n ∈ T, 0 < n ∧ n ∣ J
  /-- The certified spine. -/
  P : Finset ℕ
  /-- The spine is part of the reference word's support. -/
  P_sub : P ⊆ T
  /-- The fixed-one guards. -/
  G : Finset ℕ
  /-- The protected neutral coordinates. -/
  Nprot : Finset ℕ
  /-- Guards are compatible with the spine: they are never deleted. -/
  G_disj : Disjoint P G
  /-- Protected neutral coordinates are never deleted. -/
  N_disj : Disjoint P Nprot
  /-- The explicit zero budget. -/
  zeroBudget : ℕ
  /-- The spine fits the zero budget. -/
  budget_ok : P.card ≤ zeroBudget
  /-- Lattice step of the certified interval. -/
  g : ℤ
  /-- Lower endpoint of the certified interval. -/
  A : ℤ
  /-- Upper endpoint of the certified interval. -/
  B : ℤ
  /-- The certified reachable interval of the spine. -/
  cert : ReachesLattice (num J) P g A B
  /-- The deficit is a lattice point. -/
  deficit_lattice : g ∣ (∑ n ∈ T, num J n) - J
  /-- Exact lower mass margin. -/
  margin_lo : A ≤ (∑ n ∈ T, num J n) - J
  /-- Exact upper mass margin. -/
  margin_hi : (∑ n ∈ T, num J n) - J ≤ B

namespace GuardedBranch

variable (b : GuardedBranch)

/-- The actual mass `S(x₀)` of the complete ENTRY reference word. -/
def refMass : ℚ := ∑ n ∈ b.T, (1 : ℚ) / n

/-- The actual deficit `w = J·(S(x₀) − 1)`, as an integer. -/
def deficit : ℤ := (∑ n ∈ b.T, num b.J n) - b.J

/-- **The deficit really is `J·(S(x₀) − 1)`** — computed from the complete reference-word mass,
never from a seed mass. -/
theorem deficit_eq : (b.deficit : ℚ) = b.J * (b.refMass - 1) := by
  have hJ' : (b.J : ℚ) ≠ 0 := by
    have := b.J_pos; positivity
  have h := mass_eq_weight_div b.J_pos (S := b.T) b.T_ok
  rw [deficit, refMass]
  push_cast
  rw [h]
  field_simp

/-- **Guarded branch-to-HIT (conditional, exact).**  Under the stated hypothesis package the
actual deficit lies in the certified reachable `J`-lattice interval, hence there is an actual
subset `S` of the spine — within the zero budget, disjoint from the guards and from the protected
neutral set — whose deletion turns the same physical branch into an exact solution `S = 1`. -/
theorem guarded_branch_to_hit :
    ∃ S ⊆ b.P, S.card ≤ b.zeroBudget ∧ Disjoint S b.G ∧ Disjoint S b.Nprot ∧
      ∑ n ∈ b.T \ S, (1 : ℚ) / n = 1 := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨S, hSP, hsum⟩ :=
    b.cert b.deficit b.deficit_lattice b.margin_lo b.margin_hi
  refine ⟨S, hSP, le_trans (Finset.card_le_card hSP) b.budget_ok,
    Finset.disjoint_of_subset_left hSP b.G_disj,
    Finset.disjoint_of_subset_left hSP b.N_disj, ?_⟩
  have hST : S ⊆ b.T := hSP.trans b.P_sub
  have hJ' : (b.J : ℚ) ≠ 0 := by have := b.J_pos; positivity
  have hmass : ∑ n ∈ b.T \ S, (1 : ℚ) / n = (∑ n ∈ b.T \ S, (num b.J n : ℚ)) / b.J :=
    mass_eq_weight_div b.J_pos (fun n hn => b.T_ok n (Finset.mem_sdiff.1 hn).1)
  have hsub : ∑ n ∈ b.T \ S, (num b.J n : ℤ) = (∑ n ∈ b.T, num b.J n) - ∑ n ∈ S, num b.J n :=
    Finset.sum_sdiff_eq_sub hST
  have hval : ∑ n ∈ b.T \ S, (num b.J n : ℤ) = b.J := by
    rw [hsub, hsum, deficit]; ring
  rw [hmass]
  have : (∑ n ∈ b.T \ S, (num b.J n : ℚ)) = (b.J : ℚ) := by
    rw [← Int.cast_sum, hval]; push_cast; ring
  rw [this]
  field_simp

/-- The modified branch keeps every guard and every protected neutral coordinate. -/
theorem guards_preserved :
    ∃ S ⊆ b.P, (b.G ∩ b.T) ⊆ b.T \ S ∧ (b.Nprot ∩ b.T) ⊆ b.T \ S ∧
      ∑ n ∈ b.T \ S, (1 : ℚ) / n = 1 := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨S, hSP, _, hG, hN, hmass⟩ := b.guarded_branch_to_hit
  refine ⟨S, hSP, ?_, ?_, hmass⟩
  · intro n hn
    obtain ⟨hnG, hnT⟩ := Finset.mem_inter.1 hn
    exact Finset.mem_sdiff.2 ⟨hnT, fun hnS => (Finset.disjoint_left.1 hG hnS) hnG⟩
  · intro n hn
    obtain ⟨hnN, hnT⟩ := Finset.mem_inter.1 hn
    exact Finset.mem_sdiff.2 ⟨hnT, fun hnS => (Finset.disjoint_left.1 hN hnS) hnN⟩

end GuardedBranch

/-! ## Firewalls -/

/-- **Firewall.**  The guarded theorem is an implication about a *supplied* hypothesis package; it
does not produce a compatible ENTRY reference word. -/
theorem guarded_hit_does_not_give_entry_word :
    ¬ ∀ (H C : GuardedBranch → Prop), (∀ b, H b → C b) → ∃ b, H b := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := h (fun _ => False) (fun _ => True) (fun _ h => h.elim)
  exact hb

/-- **Firewall.**  Failure of one fixed guarded construction does not imply that no unguarded
ENTRY branch exists: from `¬P` and `P → Q` nothing follows about `Q`. -/
theorem guard_failure_does_not_kill_unguarded_branches :
    ¬ ∀ P Q : Prop, (P → Q) → ¬ P → ¬ Q := by
  intro h
  exact h False True (fun x => x.elim) not_false trivial

/-- **Counterfixture.**  The deficit must be computed from the *complete* reference-word mass.
Substituting the mass of a seed sub-word changes it: for `T = {2,3}` and seed `{2}` the masses
`5/6` and `1/2` differ. -/
theorem seed_mass_is_not_reference_mass :
    ∑ n ∈ ({2, 3} : Finset ℕ), (1 : ℚ) / n ≠ ∑ n ∈ ({2} : Finset ℕ), (1 : ℚ) / n := by
  norm_num

end GuardedBranchHit
end ResearchBankV7
end Erdos287

import Mathlib.Tactic

/-!
# Erdős #287 — Research Bank V7: exact mixed-modulus interval lifting (kernel)

INTERNAL #287 RESEARCH PROGRAMME ONLY.  **Erdős #287 is `OPEN` here and is not claimed.**

Pure finite arithmetic; every theorem of this module is kernel-proved.

All masses are measured in numerator units of one fixed final denominator `J`: a coordinate
`n ∈ T` carries the integer weight `w n` (in the application `w n = J / n`).  A *reachable* value
is a value `∑_{x ∈ S} w x` of an **actual Boolean subset** `S ⊆ T` — never merely a residue class.

* `ReachesLattice w T g A B` : every integer of the arithmetic progression `gℤ ∩ [A, B]` is the
  weight of some subset `S ⊆ T`.
* `interval_lift` : **exact mixed-modulus lifting.**  Old lattice step `g`, new step `g'` with
  `g' ∣ g` (`g` need not be a prime, `g/g'` need not be coprime to anything, and the same prime
  direction may be used repeatedly), a buffer `buf` disjoint from `T` which realizes *every*
  residue class mod `g` by an actual subset of weight in `[0, cap]`.  Then
  `ReachesLattice w (T ∪ buf) g' (A + cap) B`.
* `lift_interval_nonempty` : the overlap inequality `A + cap + g' ≤ B` makes the lifted interval
  contain a lattice point (so the lift is not vacuous).
* `chain_reaches`, `chainSupport_card_le`, `chain_mass_eq` : the exact recursion for successive
  lifts, with its support and mass bookkeeping.

**Terminology firewall.**  Failure of the overlap inequality means the *lifting certificate* is
not applicable; it is **not** an UNSAT statement about the source (`lift_failure_is_not_unsat`).
-/

namespace Erdos287
namespace ResearchBankV7
namespace IntervalLifting

open Finset

/-! ## 1.  Reachability of a lattice interval by actual Boolean subsets -/

/-- `ReachesLattice w T g A B`: every multiple of `g` in `[A, B]` is the exact weight of an actual
subset of `T`. -/
def ReachesLattice (w : ℕ → ℤ) (T : Finset ℕ) (g A B : ℤ) : Prop :=
  ∀ n : ℤ, g ∣ n → A ≤ n → n ≤ B → ∃ S ⊆ T, ∑ x ∈ S, w x = n

/-- Reachability is monotone in the ground set: enlarging the coordinate set never destroys a
certified interval (the witnessing subsets are unchanged). -/
theorem ReachesLattice.mono {w : ℕ → ℤ} {T T' : Finset ℕ} {g A B : ℤ}
    (h : ReachesLattice w T g A B) (hTT : T ⊆ T') : ReachesLattice w T' g A B := by
  intro n hg hA hB
  obtain ⟨S, hS, hsum⟩ := h n hg hA hB
  exact ⟨S, hS.trans hTT, hsum⟩

/-- Reachability is monotone in the interval. -/
theorem ReachesLattice.shrink {w : ℕ → ℤ} {T : Finset ℕ} {g A B A' B' : ℤ}
    (h : ReachesLattice w T g A B) (hA : A ≤ A') (hB : B' ≤ B) :
    ReachesLattice w T g A' B' :=
  fun n hg hA' hB' => h n hg (hA.trans hA') (hB'.trans hB)

/-! ## 2.  The exact mixed-modulus lifting theorem -/

/-- **Exact interval lifting (kernel).**

`T` already reaches the `g`-lattice interval `[A, B]`.  The buffer `buf` (disjoint from `T`)
realizes, by actual Boolean subsets, every residue class mod `g` with weight in `[0, cap]`.  Then
the union reaches the *finer* `g'`-lattice interval `[A + cap, B]`, for any `g' ∣ g`.

No coprimality is assumed: `g/g'` may share factors with `g'`, so repeated prime-power directions
are allowed. -/
theorem interval_lift {w : ℕ → ℤ} {T buf : Finset ℕ} {g g' A B cap : ℤ}
    (hdisj : Disjoint T buf)
    (hold : ReachesLattice w T g A B)
    (hbuf : ∀ r : ℤ, ∃ S ⊆ buf, (∑ x ∈ S, w x) ≡ r [ZMOD g] ∧
      0 ≤ ∑ x ∈ S, w x ∧ (∑ x ∈ S, w x) ≤ cap) :
    ReachesLattice w (T ∪ buf) g' (A + cap) B := by
  intro n _ hA hB
  obtain ⟨Sb, hSb, hres, hlo, hhi⟩ := hbuf n
  set v : ℤ := ∑ x ∈ Sb, w x with hv
  have hdvd : g ∣ n - v := Int.ModEq.dvd hres
  obtain ⟨So, hSo, hsum⟩ := hold (n - v) hdvd (by linarith) (by linarith)
  refine ⟨So ∪ Sb, Finset.union_subset_union hSo hSb, ?_⟩
  have hd : Disjoint So Sb := Finset.disjoint_of_subset_left hSo
    (Finset.disjoint_of_subset_right hSb hdisj)
  rw [Finset.sum_union hd, hsum, ← hv]
  ring

/-- **Overlap inequality ⇒ the lifted interval is not vacuous.**  If `0 < g'` and
`A + cap + g' ≤ B`, then the lifted `g'`-lattice interval contains a point. -/
theorem lift_interval_nonempty {g' A B cap : ℤ} (hg' : 0 < g') (hover : A + cap + g' ≤ B) :
    ∃ n : ℤ, g' ∣ n ∧ A + cap ≤ n ∧ n ≤ B := by
  refine ⟨g' * ((A + cap) / g' + 1), ⟨_, rfl⟩, ?_, ?_⟩
  · have h := Int.mul_ediv_add_emod (A + cap) g'
    have hlt : (A + cap) % g' < g' := Int.emod_lt_of_pos _ hg'
    nlinarith [h, hlt]
  · have h := Int.mul_ediv_add_emod (A + cap) g'
    have hnn : 0 ≤ (A + cap) % g' := Int.emod_nonneg _ (ne_of_gt hg')
    nlinarith [h, hnn, hover]

/-! ## 3.  The exact recursion for successive lifts -/

/-- One lifting stage: a buffer, the new (finer) lattice step, and the buffer's weight cap. -/
structure Stage where
  /-- The buffer coordinates of this stage. -/
  buf : Finset ℕ
  /-- The new lattice step after this stage. -/
  gNew : ℤ
  /-- The cap on the buffer weight used at this stage. -/
  cap : ℤ

/-- The support after running a chain of stages. -/
def chainSupport (T : Finset ℕ) : List Stage → Finset ℕ
  | [] => T
  | st :: rest => chainSupport (T ∪ st.buf) rest

/-- The lattice step after running a chain of stages. -/
def chainG (g : ℤ) : List Stage → ℤ
  | [] => g
  | st :: rest => chainG st.gNew rest

/-- The lower endpoint after running a chain of stages (each stage costs its cap). -/
def chainLo (A : ℤ) : List Stage → ℤ
  | [] => A
  | st :: rest => chainLo (A + st.cap) rest

/-- Validity of a chain of stages over the ground set `T` at lattice step `g`. -/
def ChainValid (w : ℕ → ℤ) (T : Finset ℕ) (g : ℤ) : List Stage → Prop
  | [] => True
  | st :: rest =>
      Disjoint T st.buf ∧
      (∀ r : ℤ, ∃ S ⊆ st.buf, (∑ x ∈ S, w x) ≡ r [ZMOD g] ∧
        0 ≤ ∑ x ∈ S, w x ∧ (∑ x ∈ S, w x) ≤ st.cap) ∧
      ChainValid w (T ∪ st.buf) st.gNew rest

/-- **Exact recursion for successive lifts (kernel).**  A valid chain of lifting stages transports
a certified lattice interval through all stages, paying one cap per stage at the lower endpoint. -/
theorem chain_reaches {w : ℕ → ℤ} {B : ℤ} :
    ∀ (L : List Stage) (T : Finset ℕ) (g A : ℤ),
      ReachesLattice w T g A B → ChainValid w T g L →
      ReachesLattice w (chainSupport T L) (chainG g L) (chainLo A L) B := by
  intro L
  induction L with
  | nil => intro T g A h _; simpa [chainSupport, chainG, chainLo] using h
  | cons st rest ih =>
      intro T g A h hvalid
      obtain ⟨hdisj, hbuf, hrest⟩ := hvalid
      have hstep : ReachesLattice w (T ∪ st.buf) st.gNew (A + st.cap) B :=
        interval_lift hdisj h hbuf
      simpa [chainSupport, chainG, chainLo] using ih (T ∪ st.buf) st.gNew (A + st.cap) hstep hrest

/-- The support of a chain is the starter together with all buffers: explicit cardinality
bound. -/
theorem chainSupport_card_le :
    ∀ (L : List Stage) (T : Finset ℕ),
      (chainSupport T L).card ≤ T.card + (L.map (fun st => st.buf.card)).sum := by
  intro L
  induction L with
  | nil => intro T; simp [chainSupport]
  | cons st rest ih =>
      intro T
      have h1 := ih (T ∪ st.buf)
      have h2 : (T ∪ st.buf).card ≤ T.card + st.buf.card := Finset.card_union_le _ _
      simp only [chainSupport, List.map_cons, List.sum_cons]
      omega

/-- Every coordinate of the chain support is either a starter coordinate or lies in one of the
buffers. -/
theorem subset_chainSupport : ∀ (L : List Stage) (T : Finset ℕ), T ⊆ chainSupport T L := by
  intro L
  induction L with
  | nil => intro T; simp [chainSupport]
  | cons st rest ih =>
      intro T
      exact (Finset.subset_union_left).trans (ih (T ∪ st.buf))

/-- **Exact mass bookkeeping.**  Under chain validity all buffers are disjoint from the running
support, so the total mass of the chain support is exactly the starter mass plus the buffer
masses. -/
theorem chain_mass_eq {w : ℕ → ℤ} (f : ℕ → ℚ) :
    ∀ (L : List Stage) (T : Finset ℕ) (g : ℤ), ChainValid w T g L →
      ∑ x ∈ chainSupport T L, f x
        = ∑ x ∈ T, f x + (L.map (fun st => ∑ x ∈ st.buf, f x)).sum := by
  intro L
  induction L with
  | nil => intro T g _; simp [chainSupport]
  | cons st rest ih =>
      intro T g hvalid
      obtain ⟨hdisj, _, hrest⟩ := hvalid
      have h1 := ih (T ∪ st.buf) st.gNew hrest
      have h2 : ∑ x ∈ T ∪ st.buf, f x = ∑ x ∈ T, f x + ∑ x ∈ st.buf, f x :=
        Finset.sum_union hdisj
      simp only [chainSupport, List.map_cons, List.sum_cons]
      rw [h1, h2]
      ring

/-! ## 4.  Terminology firewall -/

/-- **Firewall.**  Non-applicability of a lifting certificate (a violated overlap inequality) is
*not* a statement that the source is unsatisfiable: a certificate may fail while the underlying
reachability statement is true.  Here the interval `[A + cap, B]` is empty as a lattice interval
because `B < A + cap`, yet the ground set does reach the value `0`. -/
theorem lift_failure_is_not_unsat :
    ∃ (w : ℕ → ℤ) (T : Finset ℕ) (g A B cap : ℤ),
      B < A + cap ∧ (∃ S ⊆ T, ∑ x ∈ S, w x = (0 : ℤ)) ∧ ReachesLattice w T g A B := by
  refine ⟨fun _ => 0, ∅, 1, 1, 0, 5, by norm_num, ⟨∅, by simp, by simp⟩, ?_⟩
  intro n _ hA hB
  exact absurd (hA.trans hB) (by norm_num)

end IntervalLifting
end ResearchBankV7
end Erdos287

import RequestProject.Erdos287.ResearchBankV7.Numerics

/-!
# Erdős #287 — Research Bank V7: the epoch-aware verdict ledger

INTERNAL #287 RESEARCH PROGRAMME ONLY.  **Erdős #287 is `OPEN` here and is not claimed.**

Bookkeeping plus *proved* meta-statements only.  The V7 verdict scale extends the V6 one by
`FINITE-SOURCE-KILL` and `SUPERSEDED`; the V6 verdicts embed injectively (`ofV6_injective`), so
**every V6 classification is preserved verbatim** in the frozen historical block
(`v6_classifications_preserved`).

Machine-checked facts about this ledger:

* `no_closed_verdict` — no row of V7 is `CLOSED`;
* `erdos287_ownerOpen` — Erdős #287 is listed, as `OWNER-OPEN`;
* `entryOwner_ownerOpen` — the current sole owner is listed, as `OWNER-OPEN`;
* `kernelBanked_iff_kernelProof` — kernel rows are exactly those with kernel-proof evidence;
* `external_rows_never_kernel` — no row backed by an external analytic interface is kernel-banked.
-/

namespace Erdos287
namespace ResearchBankV7
namespace Ledger

open Erdos287.ResearchBankV5
open Erdos287.ResearchBankV7.Epochs

/-! ## 1.  The V7 verdict scale -/

/-- The acceptance verdict of a V7 item. -/
inductive VerdictV7
  /-- A new exact sorry-free mathematical theorem of this layer. -/
  | kernelBanked
  /-- A logical implication from an explicitly uninhabited interface. -/
  | conditionalBanked
  /-- An exact finite obstruction to an overstrong proposed theorem. -/
  | counterfixture
  /-- An exact finite contradiction killing one explicit finite source window. -/
  | finiteSourceKill
  /-- A current uninhabited research target. -/
  | ownerOpen
  /-- Bypassed or refined by later work.  **Never** means "false". -/
  | superseded
  /-- Forbidden unless a complete route to the original Erdős #287 statement is inhabited. -/
  | closed
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- The V6 verdict scale embeds into the V7 one; nothing of V6 is renamed or reinterpreted. -/
def ofV6 : ResearchBankV6.Ledger.Verdict → VerdictV7
  | .kernelBanked => VerdictV7.kernelBanked
  | .conditionalBanked => VerdictV7.conditionalBanked
  | .counterfixture => VerdictV7.counterfixture
  | .ownerOpen => VerdictV7.ownerOpen
  | .closed => VerdictV7.closed

theorem ofV6_injective : Function.Injective ofV6 := by
  intro a b h; cases a <;> cases b <;> simp_all [ofV6]

/-- An epoch-stamped ledger row: purely decidable bookkeeping data (no `Prop` payload). -/
structure RowV7 where
  /-- Human-readable item name. -/
  name : String
  /-- The epoch the item belongs to. -/
  epoch : Epoch
  /-- Acceptance verdict. -/
  verdict : VerdictV7
  /-- V5 research status (imported discipline). -/
  status : ResearchStatus
  /-- V5 evidence kind (imported discipline). -/
  evidence : EvidenceKind
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-! ## 2.  The frozen V6 block -/

/-- The V6 ledger, re-recorded verbatim with its V6 epoch stamp and its V6 verdicts. -/
def v6Frozen : List RowV7 :=
  ResearchBankV6.Ledger.v6Ledger.map fun r =>
    { name := r.name
      epoch := Epoch.v6UpperGapCarry
      verdict := ofV6 r.verdict
      status := r.status
      evidence := r.evidence }

/-- **Every V6 classification is preserved.**  Each V6 row appears in the frozen block with the
same name, status, evidence kind and (embedded) verdict. -/
theorem v6_classifications_preserved :
    ∀ r ∈ ResearchBankV6.Ledger.v6Ledger, ∃ r' ∈ v6Frozen,
      r'.name = r.name ∧ r'.verdict = ofV6 r.verdict ∧ r'.status = r.status ∧
        r'.evidence = r.evidence := by
  intro r hr
  exact ⟨_, List.mem_map_of_mem hr, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl⟩

/-- No row of the frozen V6 block is `CLOSED`. -/
theorem v6Frozen_no_closed : ∀ r ∈ v6Frozen, r.verdict ≠ VerdictV7.closed := by decide

/-! ## 3.  The new V7 rows -/

/-- The new V7 ledger rows. -/
def v7New : List RowV7 :=
  [ { name := "research epochs and meta-firewalls"
      epoch := Epoch.entryFirst
      verdict := VerdictV7.kernelBanked
      status := ResearchStatus.bank
      evidence := EvidenceKind.kernelProof }
  , { name := "bounded adaptive absorption: guarded charging (1−3γ)W ≤ 2z₀+g₀"
      epoch := Epoch.stableEntry
      verdict := VerdictV7.kernelBanked
      status := ResearchStatus.bank
      evidence := EvidenceKind.kernelProof }
  , { name := "absorption budgets at γ=1/8: W ≤ 16/5 z₀ + 8/5 g₀, U ≤ 2/5 z₀ + 1/5 g₀"
      epoch := Epoch.stableEntry
      verdict := VerdictV7.kernelBanked
      status := ResearchStatus.bank
      evidence := EvidenceKind.kernelProof }
  , { name := "branching-bit budget"
      epoch := Epoch.stableEntry
      verdict := VerdictV7.kernelBanked
      status := ResearchStatus.bank
      evidence := EvidenceKind.kernelProof }
  , { name := "fixed-polylog completion: finite second moment, disjoint buffer packing"
      epoch := Epoch.stableEntry
      verdict := VerdictV7.kernelBanked
      status := ResearchStatus.bank
      evidence := EvidenceKind.kernelProof }
  , { name := "fixed-polylog complete-row law (Croot + PNT + LLL adapter)"
      epoch := Epoch.stableEntry
      verdict := VerdictV7.conditionalBanked
      status := ResearchStatus.«open»
      evidence := EvidenceKind.conditionalInterface }
  , { name := "STABLE-ENTRY forward: ENTRY word ⟹ nonfailed terminal leaf"
      epoch := Epoch.stableEntry
      verdict := VerdictV7.kernelBanked
      status := ResearchStatus.bank
      evidence := EvidenceKind.kernelProof }
  , { name := "STABLE-ENTRY equivalence (reverse uses the external polylog interface)"
      epoch := Epoch.stableEntry
      verdict := VerdictV7.conditionalBanked
      status := ResearchStatus.«open»
      evidence := EvidenceKind.conditionalInterface }
  , { name := "exact mixed-modulus interval lifting + recursion for successive lifts"
      epoch := Epoch.exactHitSpine
      verdict := VerdictV7.kernelBanked
      status := ResearchStatus.bank
      evidence := EvidenceKind.kernelProof }
  , { name := "arithmetic-spine extraction from a supplied certificate"
      epoch := Epoch.exactHitSpine
      verdict := VerdictV7.kernelBanked
      status := ResearchStatus.bank
      evidence := EvidenceKind.kernelProof }
  , { name := "ERASURE-HIT (one-sided, fixed-part and complement forms)"
      epoch := Epoch.exactHitSpine
      verdict := VerdictV7.kernelBanked
      status := ResearchStatus.bank
      evidence := EvidenceKind.kernelProof }
  , { name := "guarded branch-to-HIT (exact, given the hypothesis package)"
      epoch := Epoch.exactHitSpine
      verdict := VerdictV7.kernelBanked
      status := ResearchStatus.bank
      evidence := EvidenceKind.kernelProof }
  , { name := "seed mass is not reference mass (counterfixture)"
      epoch := Epoch.exactHitSpine
      verdict := VerdictV7.counterfixture
      status := ResearchStatus.killed
      evidence := EvidenceKind.finiteRegressionOnly }
  , { name := "Fouvry pin-capture inequality (Fouvry/Luca–Young + Selberg + Brun–Titchmarsh)"
      epoch := Epoch.entryFirst
      verdict := VerdictV7.conditionalBanked
      status := ResearchStatus.«open»
      evidence := EvidenceKind.externalAnalyticBank }
  , { name := "branch-budget pin localization (given the numerical inputs)"
      epoch := Epoch.entryFirst
      verdict := VerdictV7.kernelBanked
      status := ResearchStatus.bank
      evidence := EvidenceKind.kernelProof }
  , { name := "finite source kills p = 2q ± 1 (59, 83, 107, 61, 73)"
      epoch := Epoch.entryFirst
      verdict := VerdictV7.finiteSourceKill
      status := ResearchStatus.bank
      evidence := EvidenceKind.finiteRegressionOnly }
  , { name := "kill pattern not universal at every prime (counterfixture)"
      epoch := Epoch.entryFirst
      verdict := VerdictV7.counterfixture
      status := ResearchStatus.killed
      evidence := EvidenceKind.finiteRegressionOnly }
  , { name := "uniform safe-prime supply for the kill pattern"
      epoch := Epoch.entryFirst
      verdict := VerdictV7.ownerOpen
      status := ResearchStatus.«open»
      evidence := EvidenceKind.researchConjecture }
  , { name := "J = L₄₄₇ has 194 decimal digits and 644 bits"
      epoch := Epoch.exactHitSpine
      verdict := VerdictV7.kernelBanked
      status := ResearchStatus.bank
      evidence := EvidenceKind.kernelProof }
  , { name := "V6 spot audit: five load-bearing statements re-exported unchanged"
      epoch := Epoch.entryFirst
      verdict := VerdictV7.kernelBanked
      status := ResearchStatus.bank
      evidence := EvidenceKind.kernelProof }
  , { name := "UpperGapCarryCompression (V6 owner)"
      epoch := Epoch.v6UpperGapCarry
      verdict := VerdictV7.superseded
      status := ResearchStatus.superseded
      evidence := EvidenceKind.researchConjecture }
  , { name := "ExactMassIntersection (V6 owner)"
      epoch := Epoch.v6UpperGapCarry
      verdict := VerdictV7.superseded
      status := ResearchStatus.superseded
      evidence := EvidenceKind.researchConjecture }
  , { name := "genuine ENTRY reference word"
      epoch := Epoch.entryFirst
      verdict := VerdictV7.ownerOpen
      status := ResearchStatus.«open»
      evidence := EvidenceKind.researchConjecture }
  , { name := "EntryFirstTerminalLeafExistenceOrKill"
      epoch := Epoch.entryFirst
      verdict := VerdictV7.ownerOpen
      status := ResearchStatus.«open»
      evidence := EvidenceKind.researchConjecture }
  , { name := "Erdős #287"
      epoch := Epoch.entryFirst
      verdict := VerdictV7.ownerOpen
      status := ResearchStatus.«open»
      evidence := EvidenceKind.researchConjecture } ]

/-- The complete V7 ledger: the frozen V6 block followed by the new rows. -/
def v7Ledger : List RowV7 := v6Frozen ++ v7New

/-! ## 4.  Machine-checked ledger discipline -/

/-- **No `CLOSED` verdict anywhere in V7.** -/
theorem no_closed_verdict : ∀ r ∈ v7Ledger, r.verdict ≠ VerdictV7.closed := by decide

/-- Erdős #287 is listed, and listed as `OWNER-OPEN`. -/
theorem erdos287_ownerOpen :
    ∃ r ∈ v7Ledger, r.name = "Erdős #287" ∧ r.verdict = VerdictV7.ownerOpen ∧
      r.status = ResearchStatus.«open» := by decide

/-- The current sole owner is listed, as `OWNER-OPEN`, in the current epoch. -/
theorem entryOwner_ownerOpen :
    ∃ r ∈ v7Ledger, r.name = "EntryFirstTerminalLeafExistenceOrKill" ∧
      r.epoch = Epoch.entryFirst ∧ r.verdict = VerdictV7.ownerOpen := by decide

/-- The node `genuine ENTRY reference word` is listed as `OWNER-OPEN`. -/
theorem entryWord_ownerOpen :
    ∃ r ∈ v7Ledger, r.name = "genuine ENTRY reference word" ∧
      r.verdict = VerdictV7.ownerOpen := by decide

/-- Kernel-banked rows are exactly the rows whose evidence kind is `kernelProof`. -/
theorem kernelBanked_iff_kernelProof :
    ∀ r ∈ v7Ledger, r.verdict = VerdictV7.kernelBanked ↔ r.evidence = EvidenceKind.kernelProof := by
  decide

/-- **No external analytic interface is ever kernel-banked.** -/
theorem external_rows_never_kernel :
    ∀ r ∈ v7Ledger, r.evidence = EvidenceKind.externalAnalyticBank →
      r.verdict = VerdictV7.conditionalBanked ∨ r.verdict = VerdictV7.ownerOpen := by decide

/-- Every non-kernel row is conditional, open, superseded, a counterfixture or a finite source
kill — never banked as proved general mathematics. -/
theorem nonKernel_rows_not_proved :
    ∀ r ∈ v7Ledger, r.evidence ≠ EvidenceKind.kernelProof →
      r.verdict = VerdictV7.conditionalBanked ∨ r.verdict = VerdictV7.ownerOpen ∨
        r.verdict = VerdictV7.counterfixture ∨ r.verdict = VerdictV7.finiteSourceKill ∨
        r.verdict = VerdictV7.superseded := by decide

/-- Superseded rows exist and are exactly the two historical V6 owners. -/
theorem superseded_rows :
    ∀ r ∈ v7New, r.verdict = VerdictV7.superseded →
      r.name = "UpperGapCarryCompression (V6 owner)" ∨
        r.name = "ExactMassIntersection (V6 owner)" := by decide

/-! ## 5.  Meta-firewalls of the ledger -/

/-- **The ledger is not a proof.**  Adding rows never inhabits a mathematical statement. -/
theorem ledger_is_not_a_proof : ¬ (∀ (_ : RowV7) (claim : Prop), claim) := by
  intro h
  exact h { name := "probe", epoch := Epoch.entryFirst, verdict := VerdictV7.ownerOpen,
            status := ResearchStatus.«open», evidence := EvidenceKind.researchConjecture } False

/-- **`SUPERSEDED` is not `false`** at ledger level either: a superseded row carries no refutation
(see `Epochs.superseded_flag_is_truth_neutral`). -/
theorem superseded_is_not_refutation :
    ∃ r : RowV7, r.verdict = VerdictV7.superseded ∧ ∃ claim : Prop, claim :=
  ⟨{ name := "superseded probe", epoch := Epoch.v6UpperGapCarry,
     verdict := VerdictV7.superseded, status := ResearchStatus.superseded,
     evidence := EvidenceKind.researchConjecture }, rfl, True, trivial⟩

/-- **Erdős #287 is not closed here.** -/
theorem erdos287_not_closed_in_v7 :
    ¬ ∃ r ∈ v7Ledger, r.name = "Erdős #287" ∧ r.verdict = VerdictV7.closed := by decide

end Ledger
end ResearchBankV7
end Erdos287
